# TiDB Cloud Lake

> TiDB Cloud Lake is a cloud-native data warehouse service for analytics workloads. It separates compute and storage, and supports ANSI SQL, semi-structured data processing, and AI-oriented workflows.

## Get Started

- [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/lake-overview.md): TiDB Cloud Lake is a cloud-native data warehouse service for analytics workloads. It separates compute and storage, and supports ANSI SQL, semi-structured data processing, and AI-oriented workflows.
- [Quick Start](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/lake-quick-start.md): Get started with TiDB Cloud Lake in three steps — sign up, initialize your lake, and explore your lake workspace.

## Guides

- Connect
  - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/connection-overview.md): TiDB Cloud Lake supports multiple connection methods to suit different use cases. All options below work with both **TiDB Cloud Lake** and **self-hosted TiDB Cloud Lake**.
  - SQL Clients
    - [LakeSQL](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/connect-using-lakesql.md): LakeSQL is a command line tool that has been designed specifically for TiDB Cloud Lake. It allows users to establish a connection with TiDB Cloud Lake and execute queries directly from a CLI window.
  - Drivers
    - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/driver-overview.md): An overview of the official drivers available for connecting to TiDB Cloud Lake.
    - [Golang](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/connect-using-golang.md): This page describes how to connect to TiDB Cloud Lake using Golang.
    - [Java](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/connect-using-java.md): This page describes how to connect to TiDB Cloud Lake using Java.
    - [Node.js](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/connect-using-node-js.md): This page describes how to connect to TiDB Cloud Lake using Node.js.
    - [Python](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/connect-using-python.md): This page describes how to connect to TiDB Cloud Lake using Python.
    - [Rust](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/connect-using-rust.md): This page describes how to connect to TiDB Cloud Lake using Rust.
  - AI Tools
    - [External AI Functions](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/external-ai-functions.md): Build powerful AI/ML capabilities by connecting TiDB Cloud Lake with your own infrastructure. External functions let you deploy custom models, leverage GPU acceleration, and integrate with any ML framework while keeping your data secure.
    - [MCP Client Integration](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/mcp-client-integration.md): Learn how to connect MCP-compatible AI tools to TiDB Cloud Lake and use session sandbox protection for safe data exploration.
    - [MCP Server](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/mcp-server.md): Learn how to install, run, and configure the TiDB Cloud Lake MCP server, including transports, safety controls, and available tools.
  - Visualization
    - [Tableau](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/tableau.md): Tableau is a visual analytics platform transforming the way we use data to solve problems. You can connect Tableau to TiDB Cloud Lake through Tableau's Other Databases (JDBC) interface by using the lake-jdbc driver.
    - [Deepnote](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/deepnote.md): Deepnote allows you to easily work on your data science projects, together in real-time and in one place with your friends and colleagues; helping you turn your ideas and analyses into products faster. Deepnote is built for the browser so you can use it across any platform (Windows, Mac, Linux or Chromebook). No downloads required, with updates shipped to you daily. All changes are instantly saved.
    - [Jupyter Notebook](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/jupyter-notebook.md): Learn how to connect Jupyter Notebook to TiDB Cloud Lake with SQLAlchemy, run queries, and visualize query results with pandas.
    - [Superset](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/superset.md): Learn how to install the TiDB Cloud Lake SQLAlchemy dialect in Apache Superset and connect Superset to a TiDB Cloud Lake warehouse.
  - Network Access
    - [Connect with AWS PrivateLink](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/connect-with-aws-privatelink.md): PrivateLink-style private endpoints offered by major clouds (AWS PrivateLink, Azure Private Link, Google Private Service Connect, etc.) let you reach TiDB Cloud Lake through private IP addresses inside your own network boundary, so no traffic has to traverse the public internet. That keeps your datasets, credentials, and admin actions on the provider's backbone and aligned with the network policies you already operate.
- Manage Resources
  - [Dashboards](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/dashboards.md): Dashboards are employed to present query results through a variety of chart types, including scorecards, pie charts, bar charts, and line charts. These charts are generated from the query results. You have the option to create a chart based on the query result after executing a query in a worksheet. Refreshing a dashboard allows you to re-execute the queries corresponding to the charts, thereby updating the charts with the latest results.
  - [Task Flow](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/task-flow.md): Task Flow is TiDB Cloud Lake's built-in workflow orchestration feature. It lets you define, schedule, and monitor SQL-based data pipelines as directed acyclic graphs (DAGs).
  - [Warehouses](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/warehouse.md): The warehouse is an essential component of TiDB Cloud Lake. A warehouse represents a set of compute resources including CPU, memory, and local caches. You must run a warehouse to perform SQL tasks.
  - [Worksheets](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/worksheet.md): Worksheets in TiDB Cloud Lake are used to organize, run, and save SQL statements. They can also be shared with others in your organization.
- Data Integration
  - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/data-integration-overview.md): The Data Integration feature in TiDB Cloud Lake provides a visual, no-code interface for importing or synchronizing data from external systems into TiDB Cloud Lake.
  - Data Sources
    - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/data-sources.md): A data source in TiDB Cloud Lake represents a connection to an external system. It stores the credentials and connection details required to access external systems and can be reused across multiple integration tasks or notification scenarios.
    - [Amazon S3 - Credentials](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/aws-credentials.md): This page describes how to create an "Amazon S3 - Credentials" data source. This data source stores the credentials required to access Amazon S3 and can be reused across multiple S3 integration tasks.
    - [Amazon SQS (S3) - IAM Role](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/amazon-sqs-s3-iam-role.md): Learn how to create an "Amazon SQS (S3) - IAM Role" data source in TiDB Cloud Lake. ![PREVIEW](https://docs-download.pingcap.com/media/images/docs/tidb-cloud/blank_transparent_placeholder.png)
    - [MySQL - Credentials](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/mysql-credentials.md): This page describes how to create a "MySQL - Credentials" data source. This data source stores the connection information required to access MySQL and can be reused across multiple MySQL integration tasks.
    - [PostgreSQL - Credentials](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/postgresql-credentials.md): This page describes how to create a "PostgreSQL - Credentials" data source. This data source stores the connection information required to access PostgreSQL and can be reused across multiple PostgreSQL integration tasks.
    - [FeiShuBot](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/feishubot.md): This page describes how to create a "FeiShuBot" data source. This data source stores a FeiShu bot webhook and message template for task failure notifications and similar scenarios.
    - [Kafka - Credentials](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/kafka-credentials.md): Create a "Kafka - Credentials" data source to store Kafka connection information for reuse in Kafka Consumer integration tasks. ![PREVIEW](https://docs-download.pingcap.com/media/images/docs/tidb-cloud/blank_transparent_placeholder.png)
  - Integration Tasks
    - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/integration-tasks.md): This page provides an overview of integration tasks in TiDB Cloud Lake. Integration tasks define how data flows from external sources into TiDB Cloud Lake, including source settings, target tables, and runtime parameters.
    - [Task Management](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/task-management.md): This page describes common operations for integration tasks, including the task creation flow, start and stop behavior, task states, and run history. For source-specific configuration, see the detailed task guides.
    - [Amazon S3 Integration Task](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/integrate-with-amazon-s3.md): The Amazon S3 data integration enables you to import files from S3 buckets into TiDB Cloud Lake. It supports CSV, Parquet, and NDJSON file formats, with options for one-time imports or continuous ingestion that automatically polls for new files.
    - [Amazon SQS (S3) Integration Task](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/integrate-with-amazon-sqs-s3.md): Learn how to create an Amazon SQS (S3) integration task that consumes S3 object creation events from an SQS queue and writes the corresponding object data into TiDB Cloud Lake. ![PREVIEW](https://docs-download.pingcap.com/media/images/docs/tidb-cloud/blank_transparent_placeholder.png)
    - [MySQL Integration Task](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/integrate-with-mysql.md): The MySQL data integration enables you to sync data from MySQL databases into TiDB Cloud Lake in real-time, with support for full snapshot loads, continuous Change Data Capture (CDC), or a combination of both.
    - [PostgreSQL Integration Task](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/integrate-with-postgresql.md): This page describes how to create a PostgreSQL integration task that synchronizes data from a PostgreSQL database into TiDB Cloud Lake.
    - [Kafka Consumer Integration Task](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/integrate-with-kafka.md): Create a Kafka Consumer task to continuously consume messages from Kafka topics and save the message content to internal object storage (tenant Stage). ![PREVIEW](https://docs-download.pingcap.com/media/images/docs/tidb-cloud/blank_transparent_placeholder.png)
- Load Data
  - Work with Stages
    - [Stage Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/stage-overview.md): A stage is a virtual location where data files reside. Files in a stage can be queried directly or loaded into a table. Alternatively, you can unload data from a table into a stage as a file.
    - [Upload to Stage](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/upload-to-stage.md): TiDB Cloud Lake recommends two file upload methods for stages PRESIGN and PUT/GET commands. These methods enable direct data transfer between the client and your storage, eliminating intermediaries and resulting in cost savings by reducing traffic between TiDB Cloud Lake and your storage.
  - Load from Files
    - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/load-from-files.md): TiDB Cloud Lake offers simple, powerful commands to load data files into tables. Most operations require just a single command.
    - [Load from Stage](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/load-from-stage.md): TiDB Cloud Lake enables you to easily import data from files uploaded to either the user stage or an internal/external stage. To do so, you can first upload the files to a stage using LakeSQL, and then employ the COPY INTO command to load the data from the staged file. Please note that the files must be in a format supported by TiDB Cloud Lake, otherwise the data cannot be imported. For more information on the file formats supported by TiDB Cloud Lake, see Input & Output File Formats.
    - [Load from Bucket](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/load-from-bucket.md): When data files are stored in an object storage bucket, such as Amazon S3, it is possible to load them directly into TiDB Cloud Lake using the COPY INTO command. Please note that the files must be in a format supported by TiDB Cloud Lake, otherwise the data cannot be imported. For more information on the file formats supported by TiDB Cloud Lake, see Input & Output File Formats.
    - [Load from Local File](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/load-from-local-file.md): Uploading your local data files to a stage or bucket before loading them into TiDB Cloud Lake can be unnecessary. Instead, you can use LakeSQL, the TiDB Cloud Lake native CLI tool, to directly import the data. This simplifies the workflow and can save you storage fees.
    - [Load from Remote File](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/load-from-remote-file.md): To load data from remote files into TiDB Cloud Lake, the COPY INTO command can be used. This command allows you to copy data from a variety of sources, including remote files, into TiDB Cloud Lake with ease. With COPY INTO, you can specify the source file location, file format, and other relevant parameters to tailor the import process to your needs. Please note that the files must be in a format supported by TiDB Cloud Lake, otherwise the data cannot be imported. For more information on the file formats supported by TiDB Cloud Lake, see Input & Output File Formats.
  - Load with Platforms
    - [Load with dbt](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/load-with-dbt.md): dbt is a transformation workflow that helps you get more work done while producing higher quality results. You can use dbt to modularize and centralize your analytics code, while also providing your data team with guardrails typically found in software engineering workflows. Collaborate on data models, version them, and test and document your queries before safely deploying them to production, with monitoring and visibility.
  - Load Semi-structured Data
    - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/load-semi-structured-data.md): Semi-structured data contains tags or markers to separate semantic elements while not conforming to rigid database structures. TiDB Cloud Lake efficiently loads these formats using the COPY INTO command, with optional on-the-fly data transformation.
    - [Load Parquet](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/load-parquet.md): Parquet is a columnar storage format commonly used in data analytics. It is designed to support complex data structures, and it is efficient for processing large datasets.
    - [Load CSV](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/load-csv.md): CSV (Comma Separated Values) is a simple file format used to store tabular data, such as a spreadsheet or database. CSV files are plain text files that contain data in a tabular format, where each row is represented on a new line, and columns are separated by a delimiter.
    - [Load TSV](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/load-tsv.md): TSV (Tab Separated Values) is a simple file format used to store tabular data, such as a spreadsheet or database. The TSV file format is very similar to CSV, the records are separated by newlines, and each field is separated by a tab. The following example shows a TSV file with two records.
    - [Load NDJSON](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/load-ndjson.md): NDJSON is built on top of JSON, and it is a strict subset of JSON. Each line must contain a separate, self-contained valid JSON object.
    - [Load ORC](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/load-orc.md): ORC (Optimized Row Columnar) is a columnar storage format commonly used in data analytics.
    - [Load Avro](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/load-avro.md): Apache Avro™ is the leading serialization format for record data, and first choice for streaming data pipelines.
  - Query & Transform
    - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/query-stage.md): TiDB Cloud Lake enables direct querying of staged files without loading data into tables first. Query files from any stage type (user, internal, external) or directly from object storage and HTTPS URLs. Ideal for data inspection, validation, and transformation before or after loading.
    - [Query Parquet Files](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/query-parquet-files-in-stage.md): Create an external stage with your own S3 bucket and credentials where your Parquet files are stored.
    - [Query CSV Files](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/query-csv-files-in-stage.md): Create an external stage with your own S3 bucket and credentials where your CSV files are stored.
    - [Query TSV Files](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/query-tsv-files-in-stage.md): Create an external stage with your own S3 bucket and credentials where your TSV files are stored.
    - [Query NDJSON Files](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/query-ndjson-files-in-stage.md): In TiDB Cloud Lake, you can directly query NDJSON files stored in stages without first loading the data into tables. This approach is particularly useful for data exploration, ETL processing, and ad-hoc analysis scenarios.
    - [Query Avro Files](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/query-avro-files-in-stage.md): TiDB Cloud Lake provides comprehensive support for querying Avro files directly from stages. This allows for flexible data exploration and transformation without needing to load the data into a table first.
    - [Query Staged ORC Files](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/query-staged-orc-files-in-stage.md): In this tutorial, we will walk you through the process of downloading the Iris dataset in ORC format, uploading it to an Amazon S3 bucket, creating an external stage, and querying the data directly from the ORC file.
    - [Transform Data on Load](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/transform-data-on-load.md): TiDB Cloud Lake's COPY INTO command allows data transformation during the loading process. This streamlines your ETL pipeline by incorporating basic transformations, eliminating the need for temporary tables.
    - [Schema Evolution](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/schema-evolution.md): Automatically evolve table schemas when loading data with COPY INTO.
  - Continuous Data Pipelines
    - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/continuous-data-pipelines.md): Build end-to-end change data capture (CDC) flows in TiDB Cloud Lake with two primitives.
    - [Track and Transform Data via Streams](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/track-and-transform-data-via-streams.md): A stream in TiDB Cloud Lake is an always-on change table every committed INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE is captured until you consume it. This page stays lean—first a quick overview, then one lab with real outputs so you can see streams in action.
    - [Automate Data Loading with Tasks](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/automate-data-loading-with-tasks.md): Tasks wrap SQL so TiDB Cloud Lake can run it for you on a schedule or when a condition is met. Keep the following knobs in mind when you define one with CREATE TASK.
- Unload Data
  - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/unload-data.md): Learn how to unload data from TiDB Cloud Lake to various file formats and storage destinations using the `COPY INTO` command.
  - [Unload Parquet File](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/unload-parquet-file.md): Learn about how to unload parquet files.
  - [Unload CSV File](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/unload-csv-file.md): Learn about how to unload CSV files.
  - [Unload TSV File](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/unload-tsv-file.md): Learn about how to unload TSV files.
  - [Unload NDJSON File](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/unload-ndjson-file.md): Learn about how to unload NDJSON files.
  - [Unload Lance Dataset](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/unload-lance-dataset.md): Learn about how to unload Lance datasets.
- Multimodal Data Analytics
  - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/multimodal-data-analytics.md): CityDrive Intelligence records video of every drive. Background processing tools split the video stream into keyframe images, extracting rich multimodal information from each image and storing it by video_id. These signals include relational metadata, JSON manifests, behavior tags, vector embeddings, and GPS traces.
  - [SQL Analytics](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/sql-analytics.md): Scenario CityDrive stages all dash-cam records into shared relational tables. This relational data (e.g., video metadata, event tags) is extracted by background processing pipelines from keyframes of the raw dash-cam video.
  - [JSON & Search](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/json-search.md): Scenario CityDrive attaches a metadata JSON payload to every extracted frame. This JSON data is extracted from video keyframes by background tools, containing rich unstructured information like scene recognition and object detection. We need to filter this JSON in TiDB Cloud Lake with Elasticsearch-style syntax without replicating it to an external system. JSON without copying it out of TiDB Cloud Lake.
  - [Vector Search](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/vector-search-guide.md): Scenario CityDrive keeps embeddings for every frame directly in TiDB Cloud Lake. These vector embeddings are the result of AI models inferencing on video keyframes to capture visual semantic features. Semantic similarity search ("find frames that look like this") can run alongside traditional SQL analytics—no separate vector service required.
  - [Geo Analytics](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/geo-analytics.md): CityDrive records precise GPS positioning and distance-to-signal for every flagged frame. This geospatial data originates from the dash-cam's GPS module and is precisely aligned with the timestamps of video keyframes. Ops teams can answer "where did this happen?" purely in SQL.
  - [Lakehouse ETL](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/lakehouse-etl.md): Scenario CityDrive's data engineering team exports every batch of dash-cam data as Parquet (videos, frame events, metadata JSON, embeddings, GPS traces, traffic light distances). These Parquet files aggregate all multimodal signals extracted from the raw video streams, forming the foundation of the warehouse. They want to update TiDB Cloud Lake's shared tables via a single COPY pipeline. to refresh the shared tables in TiDB Cloud Lake.
- Performance Tuning
  - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/performance-optimization.md): TiDB Cloud Lake primarily accelerates query performance through various indexing technologies, including data clustering, result caching, and specialized indexes, helping you significantly improve query response times.
  - [Cluster Key](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/cluster-key-performance.md): Cluster keys provide automatic data organization to dramatically improve query performance on large tables. TiDB Cloud Lake seamlessly and continually manages all clustering operations in the background - you simply define the cluster key and TiDB Cloud Lake handles the rest.
  - [Virtual Column](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/virtual-column.md): Virtual columns automatically accelerate queries on semi-structured data stored in VARIANT columns. This feature provides zero-configuration performance optimization for JSON data access.
  - [Aggregating Index](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/aggregating-index.md): Aggregating indexes dramatically accelerate analytical queries by precomputing and storing aggregation results, eliminating the need to scan entire tables for common analytics operations.
  - [Full-Text Index](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/full-text-index.md): Full-text indexes (inverted indexes) automatically enable lightning-fast text searches across large document collections by mapping terms to documents, eliminating the need for slow table scans.
  - [Ngram Index](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/ngram-index.md): Ngram indexes accelerate pattern matching queries using the LIKE operator with wildcards (%), enabling fast substring searches without full table scans.
  - [Query Result Cache](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/query-result-cache.md): TiDB Cloud Lake caches and persists the query results for every executed query when enabled. This can be used to great effect to dramatically reduce the time it takes to get an answer.
- Security & Reliability
  - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/security-reliability.md): TiDB Cloud Lake offers enterprise-grade security and reliability features that safeguard your data throughout its lifecycle. From controlling who can access your data to protecting against network threats and recovering from operational errors, TiDB Cloud Lake's multi-layered security approach helps you maintain data integrity, compliance, and business continuity.
  - Access Control
    - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/access-control.md): Learn about access control in TiDB Cloud Lake, which uses both Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and Discretionary Access Control (DAC) to manage permissions for data objects like databases, tables, and views.
    - [Privileges](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/privileges.md): A privilege is a permission to perform an action. Users must have specific privileges to execute particular actions within TiDB Cloud Lake. For example, when querying a table, a user needs SELECT privileges to the table. Similarly, to read a dataset within a stage, the user must possess READ privileges.
    - [Roles](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/roles.md): Roles in TiDB Cloud Lake play a pivotal role in simplifying the management of permissions. When multiple users require the same set of privileges, granting privileges individually can be cumbersome. Roles provide a solution by allowing the assignment of a set of privileges to a role, which can then be easily assigned to multiple users.
    - [Ownership](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/ownership.md): Ownership is a specialized privilege that signifies the exclusive rights and responsibilities a role holds over a specific data object (currently including a database, table, UDF, and stage) within TiDB Cloud Lake.
  - Data Protection Policies
    - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/data-protection-policies.md): Learn the masking policy and row access policy that safeguard sensitive information without altering stored values.
    - [Masking Policy](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/masking-policy.md): Masking policies protect sensitive data by dynamically transforming column values during query execution. They enable role-based access to confidential information—authorized users see actual data, while others see masked values.
    - [Row Access Policy](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/row-access-policy.md): Row access policies protect data by filtering table rows at query time. They let you define centralized row-level predicates once, attach them to tables, and ensure users only see rows that satisfy the policy.
  - [Audit Trail](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/audit-trail.md): TiDB Cloud Lake system history tables automatically capture detailed records of database activities, providing a complete audit trail for compliance and security monitoring.
  - [Network Policy](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/network-policy.md): Network policies control who can log in to TiDB Cloud Lake based on the client IP. Even if the credentials are correct, a connection request is rejected when its IP does not satisfy the policy, giving you an extra security layer beyond username and password.
  - [Password Policy](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/password-policy.md): Password policies define how strong a TiDB Cloud Lake password must be (length, characters, history, retry limits, and more) and how often it can change. They add predictable guardrails around every CREATE USER and password change. For the full list of attributes, see Password Policy Attributes.
  - [Authenticate with AWS IAM Role](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/authenticate-with-aws-iam-role.md): Cloud-native identity delegation (AWS IAM Role, Azure Managed Identity, Google Service Account federation, etc.) lets TiDB Cloud Lake obtain short-lived credentials to your object storage without ever handling raw access keys. That keeps data plane access inside your cloud provider's control plane while you retain ownership of every permission.
  - [Compliance & Security](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/compliance-security.md): TiDB Cloud Lake is built with security at its core, providing comprehensive protection for your data through multiple security layers, encryption standards, and compliance certifications.
  - [Fail-Safe](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/fail-safe.md): Fail-Safe refers to mechanisms aimed at recovering lost or accidentally deleted data from object storage.
  - [Recovery from Operational Errors](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/recovery-from-operational-errors.md): This guide provides step-by-step instructions for recovering from common operational errors in TiDB Cloud Lake.
- Management
  - [AI-Powered Features](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/ai-powered-features.md): With the inclusion of AI-powered features, TiDB Cloud Lake allows you to engage in natural language conversations to receive help, assistance, and solutions.
  - [Manage Costs](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/manage-costs.md): You can view the current month's consumption and billing history for your organization under Manage > Billing.
  - [Monitor Usage](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/monitor-usage.md): TiDB Cloud Lake provides monitoring functionality to help you gain a comprehensive understanding of your and your organization members' usage on the platform. To access the Monitor page, click Monitor in the sidebar menu on the homepage. The page includes the following tabs.
  - [Data Lifecycle](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/data-lifecycle.md): TiDB Cloud Lake supports familiar Data Definition Language (DDL) and Data Manipulation Language (DML) commands, making it easy for you to manage your database. Whether you're organizing, storing, querying, modifying, or deleting data, TiDB Cloud Lake follows the same industry standards you're accustomed to.
  - [Data Protection](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/data-protection.md): TiDB Cloud Lake's Continuous Data Protection (CDP) offers easy-to-use features to keep your data safe from mistakes, harmful actions, and software problems. It ensures your data can always be recovered, even if it's changed, lost, or damaged by accident or on purpose.
  - [Data Purge and Recycle](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/data-purge-and-recycle.md): In TiDB Cloud Lake, data is not immediately deleted when you run DROP, TRUNCATE, or DELETE commands. This enables TiDB Cloud Lake's time travel feature, allowing you to access previous states of your data. However, this approach means that storage space is not automatically freed up after these operations.
- [Pricing & Billing](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/pricing-billing.md): Understand the pricing model and billing details for TiDB Cloud Lake.
- [Troubleshooting](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/troubleshooting.md): This page describes how to troubleshoot common issues in TiDB Cloud Lake.

## Tutorials

- Ingest & Stream Data
  - [Ingest JSON Logs with Vector (Cloud)](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/ingest-json-logs-with-vector-cloud.md): In this tutorial, we'll simulate generating logs locally, collect them using Vector, store them in S3, and automate their ingestion into TiDB Cloud Lake using scheduled tasks.
- Migrate Data
  - [Migrate from Snowflake](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/migrate-from-snowflake.md): Migrates data from Snowflake to TiDB Cloud Lake by exporting data to Amazon S3 and loading it into TiDB Cloud Lake tables.

## Reference

- SQL Reference
  - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/sql-statements-overview.md): These topics provide reference information for various SQL commands in TiDB Cloud Lake.
  - SQL General
    - Data Types
      - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/data-types.md): TiDB Cloud Lake stores data in strongly typed columns. This page summarizes the supported data types, how automatic/explicit conversions work, and what happens with NULL or default values.
      - [Array](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array.md): Array of defined data type.
      - [Binary](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/binary.md): Variable-length sequences of raw bytes.
      - [Bitmap](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/bitmap.md): BITMAP stores membership information for unsigned 64-bit integers and supports fast set operations (count, union, intersection, etc.). SELECT statements show a binary blob, so use Bitmap Functions to interpret the values.
      - [Boolean](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/boolean.md): Basic logical data type.
      - [Date & Time](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/date-time.md): TiDB Cloud Lake's Date and Time data type supports standardization and compatibility with various SQL standards, making it easier for users migrating from other database systems.
      - [Decimal](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/decimal.md): Decimal types are high-precision numeric values to be stored and manipulated.
      - [Geospatial](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/geospatial.md): TiDB Cloud Lake stores spatial data through two data types.
      - [Interval](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/interval.md): INTERVAL represents a duration that can be written in natural-language text ('1 year 2 months', '3 days ago') or as an integer number of microseconds. TiDB Cloud Lake supports units from millennia down to microseconds and allows arithmetic on intervals, dates, and timestamps.
      - [Map](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/map.md): MAP(K, V) stores key-value pairs internally as ARRAY(TUPLE(key, value)). Define the key type K up front (Boolean, numeric, decimal, string, date, or timestamp). Keys must be non-null and unique; values can be any type, including nested structures. Use map literals ({key value}) or the MAP(keys, values) function to build a map expression.
      - [Numeric](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/numeric.md): Basic Numeric data type.
      - [String](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/string.md): Basic String data type.
      - [Tuple](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/tuple.md): Tuple is a collection of ordered, immutable types.
      - [Variant](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/variant.md): A VARIANT can store a value of any other type, including NULL, BOOLEAN, NUMBER, STRING, ARRAY, and OBJECT, and the internal value can be any level of nested structure, which is very flexible to store various data. VARIANT can also be called JSON, for more information, please refer to JSON website.
      - [Vector](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/vector.md): The VECTOR data type stores multi-dimensional arrays of 32-bit floating-point numbers, designed for machine learning, AI applications, and similarity search operations. Each vector has a fixed dimension (length) specified at creation time.
    - Information Schema
      - [Information_Schema Tables](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/information-schema-tables-overview.md): This page describes Information_Schema Tables in TiDB Cloud Lake.
      - [information_schema.columns](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/information-schema-columns-sql.md): Contains information about columns of tables.
      - [information_schema.keywords](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/information-schema-keywords-sql.md): The information_schema.keywords system table is a view that provides all keywords in TiDB Cloud Lake.
      - [information_schema.schemata](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/information-schema-schemata-sql.md): Provides metadata about all databases in the system.
      - [information_schema.tables](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/information-schema-tables-sql.md): The information_schema.tables system table is a view that provides metadata about all tables across all databases, including their schema, type, engine, and creation details. It also includes storage metrics such as data length, index length, and row count, offering insights into table structure and usage.
      - [information_schema.views](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/information-schema-views-sql.md): Provides metadata information for all views.
    - Table Engines
      - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/table-engines.md): TiDB Cloud Lake provides several table engines so that you can balance performance and interoperability needs without moving data. Each engine is optimized for a specific scenario—ranging from TiDB Cloud Lake’s native Fuse storage to external data lake formats.
      - [Fuse Engine Tables](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/fuse-engine-tables.md): TiDB Cloud Lake uses the Fuse Engine as its default storage engine, providing a Git-like data management system with.
      - [Apache Iceberg™ Tables](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/apache-icebergtm-tables.md): Learn how to connect TiDB Cloud Lake to Apache Iceberg catalogs and query or write Iceberg tables.
      - [Apache Hive Tables](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/apache-hive-tables.md): TiDB Cloud Lake can query data that is cataloged by Apache Hive without copying it. Register the Hive Metastore as a TiDB Cloud Lake catalog, point to the object storage that holds the table data, and then query the tables as if they were native TiDB Cloud Lake objects.
      - [Delta Lake Engine](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/delta-lake-engine.md): TiDB Cloud Lake's Delta Lake engine allows you to seamlessly query and analyze data in Delta Lake tables stored in your object storage. When you create a table with the Delta Lake engine in TiDB Cloud Lake, you specify a location where the data files of a Delta Lake table are stored. This setup allows you to gain direct access to the table and perform queries seamlessly from within TiDB Cloud Lake.
    - System Tables
      - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-tables.md): TiDB Cloud Lake provides a set of system tables that contain metadata about your TiDB Cloud Lake deployment, databases, tables, queries, and system performance. These tables are read-only and are automatically updated by the system.
      - [system.build_options](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-build-options.md): This system table describes the build options of the current TiDB Cloud Lake release.
      - [system.caches](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-caches.md): An overview of various caches being managed in TiDB Cloud Lake.
      - [system.clusters](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-clusters.md): Contains information about cluster nodes.
      - [system.columns](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-columns.md): Contains information about columns of tables.
      - [system.contributors](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-contributors.md): Contains information about contributors.
      - [system.copy_history](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-copy-history.md): Contains information about copy history.
      - [system.credits](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-credits.md): Contains information about credits.
      - [system.databases](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-databases.md): Provides metadata about all databases in the system, including their catalogs, names, unique IDs, owners, and drop timestamps.
      - [system.databases_with_history](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-databases-with-history.md): Records all databases, including active and dropped ones. It shows each database's catalog, name, unique ID, owner (if specified), and the deletion timestamp (NULL if still active).
      - [system.functions](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-functions.md): Contains information about the supported built-in scalar and aggregate.
      - [system.indexes](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-indexes.md): Contains information about the created indexes.
      - [system.locks](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-locks.md): Contains information about the locks in the system.
      - [system.metrics](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-metrics.md): Contains information about metric events.
      - [system.numbers](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-numbers.md): This table contains a single UInt64 column named number that contains almost all the natural numbers starting from zero.
      - [system.query_cache](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-query-cache.md): Stores information about cached query results, including details such as the query ID, result size, and the location of the cached data.
      - [system.query_log](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-query-log.md): A read-only in-memory table stores all the query logs. For the specific fields available in the query logs, refer to the Examples section.
      - [system.settings](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-settings.md): Stores the system settings of the current session.
      - [system.streams](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-streams.md): Provides information about streams in the system. Each row in this table corresponds to a stream, and the columns contain details such as the stream's mode, comment (if any), associated table name, table ID, table version, snapshot location, invalid reason (if applicable), and owner.
      - [system.table_functions](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-table-functions.md): Get all table functions' names.
      - [system.tables](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-tables-sql.md): Provides metadata information for all tables. It includes details such as table properties, creation time, number of rows, data size, and more.
      - [system.tables_with_history](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-tables-with-history.md): Provides metadata information for all tables, including historical tables. It includes details such as table properties, creation time, number of rows, data size, and more.
      - [system.temp_files](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-temp-files.md): Contains information about temporary files created by TiDB Cloud Lake, such as spill files. To remove the temporary files, use the VACUUM TEMPORARY FILES command.
      - [system.temporary_tables](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-temporary-tables.md): Provides information about all existing temporary tables in the current session.
      - [system.user_functions](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-user-functions.md): Contains information about user-defined functions and external functions in the system.
      - [system.views](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-views.md): Provides metadata information for all views.
      - [system.virtual_columns](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-virtual-columns.md): Contains information about the created virtual columns in the system.
    - System History Tables
      - [system_history.access_history](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-history-access-history.md): The fields base_objects_accessed, objects_modified, and object_modified_by_ddl are all arrays of JSON objects. Each object may include the following fields.
      - [system_history.log_history](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-history-log-history.md): Note This table contains raw log data that feeds into other specialized history tables. Other tables provide structured, query-specific views of this data.
      - [system_history.login_history](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-history-login-history.md): Login successful example sql SELECT * FROM system_history.login_history LIMIT 1;.
      - [system_history.profile_history](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-history-profile-history.md): The profiles field can be used to extract specific information. For example, to get the OutputRows value for every physical plan, the following query can be used sql SELECT jq('[.[] | {id, output_rows.statistics[4]}]', profiles) AS result FROM system_history.profile_history LIMIT 1;.
      - [system_history.query_history](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-history-query-history.md): Query the history for a specific query using its query_id.
    - [SQL Identifiers](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/sql-identifiers.md): SQL identifiers are names used for different elements within TiDB Cloud Lake, such as tables, views, and databases.
    - [Input & Output File Formats](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/input-output-file-formats.md): TiDB Cloud Lake accepts a variety of file formats both as a source and as a target for data loading or unloading. This page explains the supported file formats and their available options.
    - [Connection Parameters](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/connection-parameters.md): Connection parameters are key-value pairs you supply when creating reusable connections with CREATE CONNECTION. After a connection is created, reference it from stages, COPY commands, and other SQL features by using CONNECTION = (CONNECTION_NAME = '<connection-name>'). For full syntax and usage, see CREATE CONNECTION.
    - [SQL Dialects & Conformance](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/sql-dialects-conformance.md): This page provides details on the SQL dialects supported by TiDB Cloud Lake, along with its conformity to the SQL standard, particularly focusing on SQL2011 features and their support status within TiDB Cloud Lake.
  - SQL Statements
    - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/sql-statements-reference.md): This page moved to SQL statements overview.
    - DDL Commands
      - [DDL Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/ddl.md): These topics provide reference information for the DDL (Data Definition Language) commands in TiDB Cloud Lake.
      - Database
        - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/ddl-database-overview.md): This page provides a comprehensive overview of database operations in TiDB Cloud Lake, organized by functionality for easy reference.
        - [CREATE DATABASE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-database.md): Create a database.
        - [SHOW CREATE DATABASE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-create-database.md): Shows the CREATE DATABASE statement that creates the named database.
        - [USE DATABASE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/use-database.md): Selects a database for the current session. This statement allows you to specify and switch to a different database. Once you set the current database using this command, it remains the same until the end of the session unless you choose to change it.
        - [ALTER DATABASE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/alter-database.md): Changes the name of a database, or sets default storage options for a database.
        - [SHOW DATABASES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-databases.md): Shows the list of databases that exist on the instance.
        - [DROP DATABASE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/drop-database.md): Drops a database.
        - [SHOW DROP DATABASES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-drop-databases.md): Lists all databases along with their deletion timestamps if they have been dropped, allowing users to review deleted databases and their details.
        - [UNDROP DATABASE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/undrop-database.md): Restores the most recent version of a dropped database. This leverages the TiDB Cloud Lake Time Travel feature; a dropped object can be restored only within a retention period (defaults to 24 hours).
      - Table
        - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/ddl-table-overview.md): This page provides a comprehensive overview of table operations in TiDB Cloud Lake, organized by functionality for easy reference.
        - [CREATE TABLE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-table.md): Creating tables is one of the most complicated operations for many databases because you might need to.
        - [CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-external-table.md): The CREATE TABLE... CONNECTION = (...) statement creates a table and specifies an S3-compatible storage bucket for data storage instead of using the default local storage.
        - [CREATE TEMP TABLE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-temp-table.md): Creates a temporary table that is automatically dropped at the end of the session.
        - [CREATE TRANSIENT TABLE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-transient-table.md): Creates a table without storing its historical data for Time Travel.
        - [DROP TABLE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/drop-table.md): Deletes a table.
        - [UNDROP TABLE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/undrop-table.md): Restores the recent version of a dropped table. This leverages the TiDB Cloud Lake Time Travel feature; a dropped object can be restored only within a retention period (defaults to 24 hours).
        - [RENAME TABLE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/rename-table.md): Changes the name of a table.
        - [TRUNCATE TABLE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/truncate-table.md): Removes all data from a table while preserving the table's schema. It deletes all rows in the table, making it an empty table with the same columns and constraints. Please note that, it does not release the disk space allocated to the table.
        - [DESCRIBE TABLE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/describe-table.md): Shows information about the columns in a given table. Equivalent to SHOW FIELDS.
        - [OPTIMIZE TABLE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/optimize-table.md): Optimizing a table in TiDB Cloud Lake involves compacting or purging historical data to save storage space and enhance query performance.
        - [FLASHBACK TABLE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/flashback-table.md): Flashback a table to an earlier version with a snapshot ID or timestamp, only involving metadata operations, making it a fast process.
        - [ALTER TABLE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/alter-table.md): Use ALTER TABLE to modify the structure and properties of an existing table, including its columns, comment, storage options, external connection, or even swapping metadata with another table. The subsections below cover each supported capability.
        - [VACUUM DROP TABLE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/vacuum-drop-table.md): The VACUUM DROP TABLE command helps save storage space by permanently removing data files of dropped tables, freeing up storage space, and enabling you to manage the process efficiently. It offers optional parameters to target specific databases, preview, and limit the number of data files to be vacuumed. To list the dropped tables of a database, use SHOW DROP TABLES.
        - [VACUUM TABLE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/vacuum-table.md): The VACUUM TABLE command helps optimize system performance by freeing up storage space through the permanent removal of historical data files from a table. This includes.
        - [ATTACH TABLE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/attach-table.md): ATTACH TABLE creates a read-only link to existing table data without copying it.
        - [SHOW CREATE TABLE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-create-table.md): Shows the CREATE TABLE statement for the specified table. To include the Fuse Engine options in the result, set hide_options_in_show_create_table to 0.
        - [SHOW DROP TABLES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-drop-tables.md): Lists the dropped tables in the current or a specified database.
        - [SHOW FIELDS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-fields.md): Shows information about the columns in a given table. Equivalent to DESCRIBE TABLE.
        - [SHOW COLUMNS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-columns.md): Shows information about the columns in a given table.
        - [SHOW STATISTICS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-statistics.md): Displays statistical information about tables and their columns. Statistics help the query optimizer make better decisions about query execution plans by providing information about data distribution, row counts, and distinct values.
        - [SHOW TABLE STATUS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-table-status.md): Shows the status of the tables in a database. The status information includes various physical sizes and timestamps about a table, see Examples for details.
        - [SHOW TABLES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-tables.md): Lists the tables in the current or a specified database.
      - View
        - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/ddl-view-overview.md): This page provides a comprehensive overview of view operations in TiDB Cloud Lake, organized by functionality for easy reference.
        - [ALTER VIEW](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/alter-view.md): Alter the existing view by using another QUERY.
        - [CREATE VIEW](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-view.md): Creates a new view based on a query; the Logical View does not store any physical data, when we access a logical view, it will convert the sql into the subquery format to finish it.
        - [DROP VIEW](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/drop-view.md): Drop the view.
        - [DESC VIEW](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/desc-view.md): Returns the list of columns for a view.
        - [SHOW VIEWS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-views.md): Returns a list of view names within the specified database, or within the current database if no database name is provided.
      - User & Role
        - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/user-role.md): This page provides a comprehensive overview of user and role operations in TiDB Cloud Lake, organized by functionality for easy reference.
        - [CREATE USER](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-user.md): Creates a SQL user for connecting to TiDB Cloud Lake. Users must be granted appropriate privileges to access databases and perform operations.
        - [DESC USER](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/desc-user.md): Displays detailed information about a specific SQL user, including authentication type, roles, network policy, password policy, and other user-related settings.
        - [DROP USER](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/drop-user.md): Drop the specified user from the system.
        - [SHOW USERS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-users.md): Lists all SQL users in the system. If you're using TiDB Cloud Lake, this command also shows the user accounts (email addresses) within your organization that are used to log in to TiDB Cloud Lake.
        - [ALTER USER](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/alter-user.md): Modifies a user account, including.
        - [CREATE ROLE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-role.md): Creates a new role for access control. Roles are used to group privileges and can be assigned to users or other roles, providing a flexible way to manage permissions in TiDB Cloud Lake.
        - [SET SECONDARY ROLES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/set-secondary-roles.md): Activates all secondary roles for the current session. This means that all secondary roles granted to the user will be active, extending the user's privileges. For more information about the active role and secondary roles, see Active Role & Secondary Roles.
        - [SET ROLE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/set-role.md): Switches the active role for a session, and the currently active role can be viewed using the SHOW ROLES command, with the is_current field indicating the active role. For more information about the active role and secondary roles, see Active Role & Secondary Roles.
        - [SHOW ROLES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-roles.md): Lists all the roles assigned to the current user.
        - [DROP ROLE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/drop-role.md): Removes the specified role from the system.
        - [GRANT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/grant.md): Grants privileges, roles, and ownership for a specific database object. This includes.
        - [REVOKE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/revoke.md): Revokes privileges, roles, and ownership of a specific database object. This includes.
        - [SHOW GRANTS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-grants.md): Lists privileges granted to roles, role assignments for users, or privileges on a specific object.
      - Stage
        - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/stage.md): This page provides a comprehensive overview of stage operations in TiDB Cloud Lake, organized by functionality for easy reference.
        - [CREATE STAGE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-stage.md): Creates an internal or external stage.
        - [DROP STAGE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/drop-stage.md): Removes a stage.
        - [DESC STAGE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/desc-stage.md): Describes the properties of a stage.
        - [LIST STAGE FILES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/list-stage-files.md): Lists files in a stage.
        - [REMOVE STAGE FILES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/remove-stage-files.md): Removes files from a stage.
        - [SHOW STAGES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-stages.md): Returns a list of the created stages. The output list does not include the user stage.
        - [PRESIGN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/presign.md): Generates the pre-signed URL for a staged file by the stage name and file path you provide. The pre-signed URL enables you to access the file through a web browser or an API request.
      - Sequence
        - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/sequence.md): This page provides a comprehensive overview of sequence operations in TiDB Cloud Lake, organized by functionality for easy reference.
        - [CREATE SEQUENCE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-sequence.md): Creates a new sequence in TiDB Cloud Lake.
        - [DESC SEQUENCE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/desc-sequence.md): Describes the properties of a sequence.
        - [DROP SEQUENCE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/drop-sequence.md): Deletes an existing sequence from TiDB Cloud Lake.
        - [SHOW SEQUENCES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-sequences.md): Returns a list of the created sequences.
      - Stream
        - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/stream.md): This page provides a comprehensive overview of stream operations in TiDB Cloud Lake, organized by functionality for easy reference.
        - [CREATE STREAM](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-stream.md): Creates a stream.
        - [DESC STREAM](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/desc-stream.md): Describes the details of a specific stream.
        - [DROP STREAM](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/drop-stream.md): Deletes an existing stream.
        - [SHOW STREAMS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-streams.md): Lists the streams associated with a specific database.
      - Task
        - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/task.md): This page provides a comprehensive overview of task operations in TiDB Cloud Lake, organized by functionality for easy reference.
        - [CREATE TASK](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-task.md): The CREATE TASK statement is used to define a new task that executes a specified SQL statement on a scheduled basis or dag based task graph.
        - [ALTER TASK](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/alter-task.md): The ALTER TASK statement is used to modify an existing task.
        - [DROP TASK](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/drop-task.md): The DROP TASK statement is used to delete an existing task.
        - [EXECUTE TASK](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/execute-task.md): The EXECUTE TASK statement is used to execute an existing task manually.
        - [SHOW TASKS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-tasks.md): Lists the tasks that are visible to the current role.
        - [TASK ERROR NOTIFICATION PAYLOAD](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/task-error-notification-payload.md): The payload body for task error notification.
      - Notification
        - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/notification.md): This page provides a comprehensive overview of Notification operations in TiDB Cloud Lake, organized by functionality for easy reference.
        - [CREATE NOTIFICATION INTEGRATION](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-notification-integration.md): Creates a named notification integration that can be used to send notifications to external messaging services.
        - [ALTER NOTIFICATION INTEGRATION](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/alter-notification-integration.md): Alter the settings of a named notification integration that can be used to send notifications to external messaging services.
        - [DROP NOTIFICATION INTEGRATION](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/drop-notification-integration.md): The DROP NOTIFICATION INTEGRATION statement is used to delete an existing notification.
        - [DESCRIBE NOTIFICATION INTEGRATION](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/describe-notification-integration.md): Shows the properties of a notification integration.
      - Tag
        - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/tag-overview.md): Overview of tag management and assignment in TiDB Cloud Lake.
        - [CREATE TAG](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-tag.md): Creates a new tag with optional allowed values and comment.
        - [DROP TAG](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/drop-tag.md): Removes a tag. A tag cannot be dropped if it is still referenced by any object.
        - [SHOW TAGS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-tags.md): Lists tag definitions in the current tenant.
        - [SET TAG](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/set-tag.md): Assigns or removes tags on database objects.
      - Connection
        - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/connection.md): A connection in TiDB Cloud Lake refers to a designated configuration that encapsulates the details required to interact with an external storage service. It serves as a centralized and reusable set of parameters, such as access credentials, endpoint URLs, and storage types, facilitating the integration of TiDB Cloud Lake with various storage services.
        - [CREATE CONNECTION](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-connection.md): Creates a connection to external storage.
        - [DESC CONNECTION](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/desc-connection.md): Describes the details of a specific connection, providing information about its type and configuration.
        - [DROP CONNECTION](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/drop-connection.md): Deletes an existing connection.
        - [SHOW CONNECTIONS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-connections.md): Displays a list of all available connections.
      - Catalog
        - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/catalog.md): An overview of Catalog operations in TiDB Cloud Lake.
        - [SHOW CATALOGS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-catalogs.md): Lists catalogs.
        - [SHOW CREATE CATALOG](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-create-catalog.md): Shows catalog definition information.
      - File Format
        - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/file-format.md): This page provides a comprehensive overview of File Format operations in TiDB Cloud Lake, organized by functionality for easy reference.
        - [CREATE FILE FORMAT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-file-format.md): Create a named file format.

        - [SHOW FILE FORMATS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-file-formats.md): Returns a list of created file formats.
      - Cluster Key
        - [ALTER CLUSTER KEY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/alter-cluster-key.md): Changes the cluster key for a table.
        - [DROP CLUSTER KEY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/drop-cluster-key.md): Deletes the cluster key for a table.
        - [RECLUSTER TABLE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/recluster-table.md): Re-clusters a table. For why and when to re-cluster a table, see Re-clustering Table.
        - [SET CLUSTER KEY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/set-cluster-key.md): Set a cluster key when creating a table.
        - [Cluster Key](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/cluster-key.md): This page provides a comprehensive overview of cluster key operations in TiDB Cloud Lake, organized by functionality for easy reference.
      - Aggregating Index
        - [CREATE AGGREGATING INDEX](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-aggregating-index.md): Create a new aggregating index in TiDB Cloud Lake.
        - [DROP AGGREGATING INDEX](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/drop-aggregating-index.md): Deletes an existing aggregating index. Please note that deleting an aggregating index does NOT remove the associated storage blocks. To delete the blocks as well, use the VACUUM TABLE command. To disable the aggregating indexing feature, set enable_aggregating_index_scan to 0.
        - [Aggregating Index](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/aggregating-index-sql.md): This page provides a comprehensive overview of aggregating index operations in TiDB Cloud Lake, organized by functionality for easy reference.
        - [REFRESH AGGREGATING INDEX](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/refresh-aggregating-index.md): TiDB Cloud Lake automatically maintains aggregating indexes in SYNC mode as new data is ingested. Run REFRESH AGGREGATING INDEX when you introduce an index on a table that already contains data so earlier rows are backfilled.
      - Inverted Index
        - [CREATE INVERTED INDEX](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-inverted-index.md): Creates a new inverted index in TiDB Cloud Lake.
        - [DROP INVERTED INDEX](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/drop-inverted-index.md): Removes an inverted index in TiDB Cloud Lake.
        - [Inverted Index](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/inverted-index.md): This page provides a comprehensive overview of inverted index operations in TiDB Cloud Lake, organized by functionality for easy reference.
        - [REFRESH INVERTED INDEX](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/refresh-inverted-index.md): TiDB Cloud Lake automatically refreshes inverted indexes in SYNC mode whenever new data is written. Use REFRESH INVERTED INDEX primarily to backfill rows that existed before the index was declared.
      - Ngram Index
        - [CREATE NGRAM INDEX](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-ngram-index.md): Creates an Ngram index on a column for a table.
        - [DROP NGRAM INDEX](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/drop-ngram-index.md): Drops an existing NGRAM index from a table.
        - [Ngram Index](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/ngram-index-sql.md): This page provides a comprehensive overview of Ngram index operations in TiDB Cloud Lake, organized by functionality for easy reference.
        - [REFRESH NGRAM INDEX](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/refresh-ngram-index.md): TiDB Cloud Lake automatically refreshes NGRAM indexes when data is ingested. Use REFRESH NGRAM INDEX when you need to backfill data that existed before the index was defined.
      - Spatial Index
        - [Spatial Index](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/spatial-index-overview.md): Spatial indexes accelerate spatial predicate filtering on `GEOMETRY` columns.
        - [CREATE SPATIAL INDEX](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-spatial-index.md): Creates a new spatial index in TiDB Cloud Lake.
        - [REFRESH SPATIAL INDEX](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/refresh-spatial-index.md): Refreshes a spatial index to backfill historical rows or update the index after data changes.
        - [DROP SPATIAL INDEX](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/drop-spatial-index.md): Removes a spatial index in TiDB Cloud Lake.
      - Vector Index
        - [CREATE VECTOR INDEX](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-vector-index.md): Creates a Vector index on a VECTOR column for a table to enable efficient similarity search using the HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) algorithm.
        - [DROP VECTOR INDEX](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/drop-vector-index.md): Removes a Vector index from a table.
        - [Vector Index](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/vector-index.md): Vector indexes in TiDB Cloud Lake enable efficient similarity search on high-dimensional vector data using the HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) algorithm. They support use cases like semantic search, recommendation systems, and AI applications.
        - [REFRESH VECTOR INDEX](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/refresh-vector-index.md): Builds a Vector index for existing data that was inserted before the index was created.
      - Virtual Column
        - [Virtual Column](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/virtual-column-overview.md): This page provides a comprehensive overview of virtual column operations in TiDB Cloud Lake, organized by functionality for easy reference.
        - [REFRESH VIRTUAL COLUMN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/refresh-virtual-column.md): The REFRESH VIRTUAL COLUMN command in TiDB Cloud Lake is used to explicitly trigger the creation of virtual columns for existing tables. While TiDB Cloud Lake automatically manages virtual columns for new data, there are specific scenarios where manual refreshing is necessary to take full advantage of this feature.
        - [SHOW VIRTUAL COLUMNS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-virtual-columns.md): Shows the created virtual columns in the system. Equivalent to SELECT * FROM system.virtual_columns.
      - User-Defined Function
        - [User-Defined Function](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/user-defined-function.md): User-Defined Functions (UDFs) in TiDB Cloud Lake allow you to create custom operations tailored to your specific data processing needs. This page highlights the commands you will use most often and helps you choose the right function type for your use case.
        - [Choose a User-Defined Function Type](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/choose-a-udf-type.md): Learn how to choose a SQL, aggregate, table, or external UDF in TiDB Cloud Lake based on return shape, runtime, and operations.
        - [ALTER FUNCTION](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/alter-function.md): Alters a user-defined function. Supports all function types Scalar SQL, Tabular SQL, and Embedded functions.
        - [CREATE AGGREGATE FUNCTION](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-aggregate-function.md): Creates a user-defined aggregate function (UDAF) that runs inside TiDB Cloud Lake's JavaScript or Python runtime.
        - [CREATE SCALAR FUNCTION](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-scalar-function.md): Creates a scalar user-defined function (Scalar UDF). The same CREATE FUNCTION statement supports two implementation styles.
        - [CREATE TABLE FUNCTION](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-table-function.md): Creates a tabular SQL UDF (UDTF) that encapsulates SQL queries as a table function. Table functions are written in SQL; no external languages are involved.
        - [DROP FUNCTION](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/drop-function.md): Drops a user-defined function. Works with all function types Scalar SQL, Tabular SQL, and Embedded functions.
        - [SHOW USER FUNCTIONS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-user-functions.md): Lists all user-defined functions including scalar functions, table functions, embedded functions, and external functions.
      - External Function
        - [External Function](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/external-function.md): This page provides a comprehensive overview of External Function operations in TiDB Cloud Lake, organized by functionality for easy reference.
        - [CREATE FUNCTION](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-function.md): Creates an external function that calls a remote handler over Flight (typically Python or other services).
        - [ALTER FUNCTION](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/alter-function-sql.md): Alters an external function.
        - [DROP FUNCTION](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/drop-function-sql.md): Drops an external function.
      - Masking Policy
        - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/masking-policy-sql.md): This page provides a comprehensive overview of Masking Policy operations in TiDB Cloud Lake, organized by functionality for easy reference.
        - [CREATE MASKING POLICY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-masking-policy.md): Creates a new masking policy in TiDB Cloud Lake.
        - [DESC MASKING POLICY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/desc-masking-policy.md): Displays detailed information about a specific masking policy in TiDB Cloud Lake.
        - [DROP MASKING POLICY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/drop-masking-policy.md): Deletes an existing masking policy from TiDB Cloud Lake. When you drop a masking policy, it is removed from TiDB Cloud Lake, and its associated masking rules are no longer in effect. Please note that, before dropping a masking policy, ensure that this policy is not associated with any columns.
      - Network Policy
        - [ALTER NETWORK POLICY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/alter-network-policy.md): Modifies an existing network policy in TiDB Cloud Lake.
        - [CREATE NETWORK POLICY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-network-policy.md): Creates a new network policy in TiDB Cloud Lake.
        - [DESC NETWORK POLICY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/desc-network-policy.md): Displays detailed information about a specific network policy in TiDB Cloud Lake. It provides information about the allowed and blocked IP address lists associated with the policy and the comment, if any, that describes the purpose or function of the policy.
        - [DROP NETWORK POLICY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/drop-network-policy.md): Deletes an existing network policy from TiDB Cloud Lake. When you drop a network policy, it is removed from TiDB Cloud Lake, and its associated rules for allowed and blocked IP address lists are no longer in effect. Please note that, before dropping a network policy, ensure that this policy is not associated with any users.
        - [SHOW NETWORK POLICIES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-network-policies.md): Displays a list of all existing network policies in TiDB Cloud Lake. It provides information about the available network policies, including their names and whether they have any allowed or blocked IP address lists configured.
        - [Network Policy](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/network-policy-sql.md): This page provides a comprehensive overview of Network Policy operations in TiDB Cloud Lake, organized by functionality for easy reference.
      - Password Policy
        - [ALTER PASSWORD POLICY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/alter-password-policy.md): Modifies an existing password policy in TiDB Cloud Lake.

        - [DROP PASSWORD POLICY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/drop-password-policy.md): Deletes an existing password policy from TiDB Cloud Lake. Please note that, before dropping a password policy, ensure that this policy is not associated with any users.
        - [Password Policy](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/password-policy-sql.md): This page provides a comprehensive overview of Password Policy operations in TiDB Cloud Lake, organized by functionality for easy reference.
        - [SHOW PASSWORD POLICIES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-password-policies.md): Displays a list of all existing password policies in TiDB Cloud Lake.
      - Row Access Policy
        - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/row-access-policy-overview.md): A comprehensive overview of Row Access Policy operations in TiDB Cloud Lake, organized by functionality for easy reference.
        - [CREATE ROW ACCESS POLICY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-row-access-policy.md): Creates a new row access policy in TiDB Cloud Lake. A row access policy defines a Boolean predicate that TiDB Cloud Lake applies to rows when the policy is attached to a table.
        - [DESC ROW ACCESS POLICY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/desc-row-access-policy.md): Displays detailed information about a specific row access policy in TiDB Cloud Lake.
        - [DROP ROW ACCESS POLICY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/drop-row-access-policy.md): Deletes an existing row access policy from TiDB Cloud Lake. Before dropping a policy, detach it from all tables that reference it.
      - Dictionary
        - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/dictionary.md): An overview of dictionary management and information commands.

      - Pipe
        - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/pipe.md): Pipe-related SQL commands for ingestion pipelines in TiDB Cloud Lake.
        - [CREATE PIPE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-pipe.md): Learn how to use the CREATE PIPE command for ingestion pipelines in TiDB Cloud Lake.

      - Transaction
        - [BEGIN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/begin.md): Starts a new transaction. BEGIN and COMMIT/ROLLBACK must be used together to start and then either save or undo a transaction.
        - [COMMIT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/commit.md): Saves all changes made during a transaction. BEGIN and COMMIT/ROLLBACK must be used together to start and then either save or undo a transaction.
        - [Transaction](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/transaction.md): This page provides a comprehensive overview of Transaction operations in TiDB Cloud Lake, organized by functionality for easy reference.
        - [ROLLBACK](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/rollback.md): Undoes all changes made during a transaction. BEGIN and COMMIT/ROLLBACK must be used together to start and then either save or undo a transaction.
        - [SHOW LOCKS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-locks.md): Provides a list of active transactions currently holding locks on tables, either for the current user across all their sessions or for all users within the TiDB Cloud Lake system. A lock is a synchronization mechanism that restricts access to shared resources, such as tables, ensuring orderly and controlled interactions among processes or threads within the TiDB Cloud Lake system to maintain data consistency and prevent conflicts.
      - Variable
        - [SQL Variables](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/sql-variables.md): SQL variables allow you to store and manage temporary data within a session, making scripts more dynamic and reusable.
