        - [SET VARIABLE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/set-variable.md): Sets the value of one or more SQL variables within a session. The values can be simple constants, expressions, query results, or database objects. Variables persist for the duration of your session and can be used in subsequent queries.
        - [SHOW VARIABLES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-variables.md): Displays all session variables and their details, such as names, values, and types.
        - [UNSET VARIABLE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/unset-variable.md): Removes one or more variables from the current session.
      - Stored Procedure
        - [CALL PROCEDURE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/call-procedure.md): Executes a stored procedure by calling its name, optionally passing arguments if the procedure requires them.
        - [CREATE PROCEDURE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-procedure.md): Defines a stored procedure that executes SQL operations and returns a result.
        - [DESC PROCEDURE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/desc-procedure.md): Displays detailed information about a specific stored procedure.
        - [DROP PROCEDURE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/drop-procedure.md): Deletes an existing stored procedure.
        - [Stored Procedure](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/stored-procedure.md): This page provides a comprehensive overview of Stored Procedure operations in TiDB Cloud Lake, organized by functionality for easy reference.
        - [SHOW PROCEDURES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-procedures.md): Returns a list of all stored procedures in the system.
      - Warehouse
        - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/warehouse-overview.md): Warehouse-related SQL commands for TiDB Cloud Lake.
        - [CREATE WAREHOUSE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-warehouse.md): Creates a new warehouse for compute resources.
        - [USE WAREHOUSE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/use-warehouse.md): Binds the current session to a specific warehouse. Subsequent queries in the session will use this warehouse for execution.
        - [SHOW WAREHOUSES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-warehouses.md): Lists all warehouses visible to the current tenant.
        - [ALTER WAREHOUSE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/alter-warehouse.md): Suspends, resumes, or modifies settings of an existing warehouse.
        - [ALTER WAREHOUSE ASSIGN NODES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/alter-warehouse-assign-nodes.md): Learn how to use the ALTER WAREHOUSE ASSIGN NODES command to assign nodes to clusters in a warehouse in TiDB Cloud Lake.
        - [ALTER WAREHOUSE UNASSIGN NODES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/alter-warehouse-unassign-nodes.md): Learn how to use the ALTER WAREHOUSE UNASSIGN NODES command to remove assigned nodes from clusters in a warehouse in TiDB Cloud Lake.
        - [DROP WAREHOUSE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/drop-warehouse.md): Removes a warehouse and frees up the resources associated with it.
        - [QUERY_HISTORY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/query-history.md): Retrieves query execution logs for analysis and monitoring purposes.
      - Worker
        - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/worker-overview.md): Worker-related SQL commands for deployments with cloud control enabled.
        - [CREATE WORKER](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-worker.md): Creates a worker with an optional key-value option list.
        - [ALTER WORKER](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/alter-worker.md): Modify worker tags, options, or state with ALTER WORKER.
        - [DROP WORKER](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/drop-worker.md): Remove a worker with DROP WORKER.
        - [SHOW WORKERS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-workers.md): List workers and their metadata with SHOW WORKERS.
        - [Worker Examples](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/worker-examples.md): Comprehensive examples of using WORKER commands to manage UDF execution environments in TiDB Cloud Lake.
      - Workload Group
        - [Workload Group](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/workload-group.md): Workload groups enable resource management and query concurrency control in TiDB Cloud Lake by allocating CPU, memory quotas and limiting concurrent queries for different user groups.
        - [ALTER WORKLOAD GROUP](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/alter-workload-group.md): Update a workload group with specified quota settings.
        - [CREATE WORKLOAD GROUP](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-workload-group.md): Creates a workload group with specified quota settings. Workload groups control resource allocation and query concurrency by binding to users. When a user submits queries, the workload group limits are applied based on the user's assigned group.
        - [DROP WORKLOAD GROUP](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/drop-workload-group.md): Removes the specified workload group.
        - [RENAME WORKLOAD GROUP](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/rename-workload-group.md): Renames an existing workload group to a new name.
        - [SHOW WORKLOAD GROUPS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-workload-groups.md): Returns a list of all existing workload groups along with their quotas.
      - Table Versioning
        - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/table-versioning.md): Table versioning lets you create named references to specific snapshots of a FUSE table. These references survive automatic retention cleanup, giving you stable, human-readable pointers to historical table states.
        - [CREATE SNAPSHOT TAG](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/create-snapshot-tag.md): Creates a named snapshot tag on a FUSE table, allowing you to bookmark and query specific points in the table's history.
        - [DROP SNAPSHOT TAG](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/drop-snapshot-tag.md): Drops a named snapshot tag from a FUSE table, allowing the referenced snapshot to be garbage collected if no other tags or retention policies protect it.
    - DML Commands
      - [DML Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/dml.md): This page provides reference information for the DML (Data Manipulation Language) commands in TiDB Cloud Lake.
      - [`COPY INTO <location>`](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/copy-into-location.md): COPY INTO allows you to unload data from a table or query into one or more files in one of the following locations.
      - [`COPY INTO <table>`](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/copy-into-table.md): COPY INTO allows you to load data from files located in one of the following locations.
      - [DELETE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/delete.md): Removes one or more rows from a table.
      - [INSERT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/insert.md): Inserts one or more rows into a table.
      - [INSERT (multi-table)](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/insert-multi-table.md): Inserts rows into multiple tables in a single transaction, with the option for the insertion to be dependent on certain conditions (conditionally) or to occur regardless of any conditions (unconditionally).
      - [MERGE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/merge.md): Performs INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE operations on rows within a target table, all in accordance with conditions and matching criteria specified within the statement, using data from a specified source.
      - [REPLACE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/replace.md): REPLACE INTO can either insert multiple new rows into a table or update existing rows if those rows already exist, using the following sources of data.
      - [UPDATE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/update.md): Updates rows in a table with new values, optionally using values from other tables.
    - Query Syntax
      - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/query-syntax.md): This page provides reference information for the query syntax in TiDB Cloud Lake. Each component can be used individually or combined to build powerful queries.
      - [SELECT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/select.md): Retrieves data from a table.
      - [AT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/at.md): The AT clause enables you to retrieve previous versions of your data by specifying a snapshot ID, timestamp, stream name, or a time interval.
      - [JOIN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/join.md): Joins combine columns from two or more tables into one result set. TiDB Cloud Lake implements both ANSI SQL joins and Lake-specific extensions, allowing you to work with dimensional data, slowly changing facts, and time-series streams using the same syntax.
      - [PIVOT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/pivot.md): The PIVOT operation in TiDB Cloud Lake allows you to transform a table by rotating it and aggregating results based on specified columns.
      - [UNPIVOT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/unpivot.md): The UNPIVOT operation rotates a table by transforming columns into rows.
      - [GROUP BY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/group-by.md): TiDB Cloud Lake supports GROUP BY with a variety of extensions.
      - [CHANGES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/changes.md): The CHANGES clause allows querying the change tracking metadata for a table within a defined time interval. Please note that the time interval must fall within the data retention period (defaulted to 24 hours). To define a time interval, use the AT keyword to specify a time point as the start of the interval, with the current time being applied as the default end of the interval. If you wish to specify a past time as the end of the interval, use the END keyword in conjunction with the AT keyword to set the interval.
      - [QUALIFY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/qualify.md): QUALIFY is a clause used to filter the results of a window function. Therefore, to successfully utilize the QUALIFY clause, there must be at least one window function in the SELECT list or the QUALIFY clause (See Examples for each case). In other words, QUALIFY is evaluated after window functions are computed. Here’s the typical order of execution for a query with a QUALIFY statement clause.
      - [SETTINGS Clause](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/settings-clause.md): The SETTINGS clause configures specific settings that influence the execution behavior of the SQL statement it precedes. To view the available settings in TiDB Cloud Lake and their values, use SHOW SETTINGS.
      - [TOP](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/top.md): Limits the maximum number of rows returned by a query.
      - [VALUES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/values.md): The VALUES clause creates an inline table by explicitly defining rows of data. This temporary table can be used directly or within other SQL statements.
      - [WITH Clause](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/clause.md): The WITH clause is an optional clause that precedes the body of the SELECT statement, and defines one or more CTEs (common table expressions) that can be referenced later in the statement.
      - [WITH CONSUME](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/with-consume.md): Consumes data from a stream within a SELECT query.
      - [WITH Stream Hints](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/stream-hints.md): Specifies various stream configuration options using hints to control how the stream is processed.
    - Query Operators
      - [Arithmetic Operators](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/arithmetic-operators.md): This page describes Arithmetic Operators in TiDB Cloud Lake.
      - [Comparison Operators](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/comparison-operators.md): This page describes Comparison Operators in TiDB Cloud Lake.
      - [Query Operators](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/query-operators.md): This page provides reference information for the query operators in TiDB Cloud Lake.
      - [JSON Operators](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/json-operators.md): This page describes JSON Operators in TiDB Cloud Lake.
      - [Logical Operators](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/logical-operators.md): This page describes Logical Operators in TiDB Cloud Lake.
      - [Set Operators](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/set-operators-sql.md): Set operators combine the results of two queries into a single result. TiDB Cloud Lake supports the following set operators.
      - [Subquery Operators](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/subquery-operators.md): A subquery is a query nested within another one. TiDB Cloud Lake supports the following subquery types.
    - Explain Commands
      - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/explain-commands.md): This page provides reference information for the explain-related commands in TiDB Cloud Lake.
      - [EXPLAIN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/explain.md): Shows the execution plan of a SQL statement. An execution plan is shown as a tree consisting of different operators where you can see how TiDB Cloud Lake will execute the SQL statement. An operator usually includes one or more fields describing the actions TiDB Cloud Lake will perform or the objects related to the query.
      - [EXPLAIN ANALYZE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/explain-analyze.md): EXPLAIN ANALYZE used to display a query execution plan along with actual run-time performance statistics.
      - [EXPLAIN ANALYZE GRAPHICAL](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/explain-analyze-graphical.md): Analyzes query performance with an interactive visual representation in your browser. Available exclusively in LakeSQL v0.22.2+.
      - [EXPLAIN AST](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/explain-ast.md): Returns the abstract syntax tree (AST) of an SQL statement. The command breaks an SQL statement into syntactic parts and represents them in a hierarchical structure.
      - [EXPLAIN PERF](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/explain-perf.md): Profiles query CPU usage and returns an HTML flame graph collected from all cluster nodes.
      - [EXPLAIN RAW](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/explain-raw.md): Shows the logical execution plan of an SQL statement that you can use to analyze, troubleshoot, and improve the efficiency of your queries.
      - [EXPLAIN SYNTAX](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/explain-syntax.md): Outputs formatted SQL code. This command works as an SQL formatter that makes your code easy to read.
    - Administration Commands
      - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/administration-commands.md): This page provides reference information for the system administration commands in TiDB Cloud Lake.
      - [KILL](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/kill.md): Forcibly terminates the currently running queries.
      - [SET](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/set.md): Changes the value of a system setting for the current session. To show all the current settings, use SHOW SETTINGS.
      - [UNSET](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/unset.md): Reverts one or more system settings to their global or default levels and values. For more information about the setting levels, see Setting Levels. To show all the current settings, use SHOW SETTINGS.
      - [SET_VAR](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/set-var.md): SET_VAR is used to specify optimizer hints within a single SQL statement, allowing for finer control over the execution plan of that specific statement. This includes.
      - [SHOW SETTINGS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-settings.md): TiDB Cloud Lake provides a variety of system settings that enable you to control how TiDB Cloud Lake works. This command displays the current and default values, as well as the Setting Levels, of available system settings. To update a setting, use the SET or UNSET command.
      - [SHOW INDEXES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-indexes.md): Shows the created indexes. Equivalent to SELECT * FROM system.indexes.
      - [SHOW FUNCTIONS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-functions.md): Lists the currently supported built-in scalar and aggregate functions.
      - [SHOW USER FUNCTIONS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-user-functions-sql.md): Lists the existing user-defined functions and external functions in the system. Equivalent to SELECT name, is_aggregate, description, arguments, language FROM system.user_functions....
      - [SHOW TABLE FUNCTIONS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-table-functions.md): Shows the list of supported table functions currently.
      - [SHOW PROCESSLIST](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-processlist.md): The TiDB Cloud Lake process list indicates the operations currently being performed by the set of threads executed within the server.
      - [SHOW METRICS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-metrics.md): Shows the list of system metrics.
      - [VACUUM DROP TABLE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/vacuum-drop-table-sql.md): This page describes VACUUM DROP TABLE in TiDB Cloud Lake.
      - [VACUUM TABLE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/vacuum-table-sql.md): This page describes VACUUM TABLE in TiDB Cloud Lake.
      - [VACUUM TEMPORARY FILES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/vacuum-temporary-files.md): Removes temporary files created by TiDB Cloud Lake, such as spill files.
      - [VACUUM VIRTUAL COLUMN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/vacuum-virtual-column.md): Removes obsolete virtual column files for a table.
      - [EXECUTE IMMEDIATE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/execute-immediate.md): Executes a SQL script. For how to write SQL scripts for TiDB Cloud Lake, see Stored Procedure & SQL Scripting.
      - [SYSTEM FLUSH PRIVILEGES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-flush-privileges.md): Broadcasts a privilege metadata refresh to all query nodes so GRANT and REVOKE changes take effect immediately.
      - [SYSTEM ENABLE / DISABLE EXCEPTION_BACKTRACE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-enable-disable-exception-backtrace.md): Controls the generation of Rust backtraces in TiDB Cloud Lake. SYSTEM ENABLE EXCEPTION_BACKTRACE enables backtraces for debugging purposes when a panic occurs, while SYSTEM DISABLE EXCEPTION_BACKTRACE disables them to avoid additional overhead or exposure of sensitive information.
  - SQL Functions
    - [SQL Function Reference](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/sql-function-reference.md): TiDB Cloud Lake provides comprehensive SQL functions for all types of data processing. Functions are organized by importance and usage frequency.
    - Bitmap Functions
      - [BITMAP_AND](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/bitmap-and.md): Performs a bitwise AND operation on the two bitmaps.
      - [BITMAP_AND_COUNT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/bitmap-and-count.md): Counts the number of bits set to 1 in the bitmap by performing a logical AND operation.
      - [BITMAP_AND_NOT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/bitmap-and-not.md): Alias for BITMAP_NOT.
      - [BITMAP_CARDINALITY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/bitmap-cardinality.md): Alias for BITMAP_COUNT.
      - [BITMAP_CONTAINS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/bitmap-contains.md): Checks if the bitmap contains a specific value.
      - [BITMAP_COUNT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/bitmap-count.md): Counts the number of bits set to 1 in the bitmap.
      - [BITMAP_HAS_ALL](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/bitmap-has-all.md): Checks if the first bitmap contains all the bits in the second bitmap.
      - [BITMAP_HAS_ANY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/bitmap-has-any.md): Checks if the first bitmap has any bit matching the bits in the second bitmap.
      - [BITMAP_INTERSECT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/bitmap-intersect.md): Counts the number of bits set to 1 in the bitmap by performing a logical INTERSECT operation.
      - [BITMAP_MAX](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/bitmap-max.md): Gets the maximum value in the bitmap.
      - [BITMAP_MIN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/bitmap-min.md): Gets the minimum value in the bitmap.
      - [BITMAP_NOT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/bitmap-not.md): Generates a new bitmap with elements from the first bitmap that are not in the second one.
      - [BITMAP_NOT_COUNT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/bitmap-not-count.md): Counts the number of bits set to 0 in the bitmap by performing a logical NOT operation.
      - [BITMAP_OR](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/bitmap-or.md): Performs a bitwise OR operation on the two bitmaps.
      - [BITMAP_OR_COUNT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/bitmap-or-count.md): Counts the number of bits set to 1 in the bitmap by performing a logical OR operation.
      - [BITMAP_SUBSET_IN_RANGE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/bitmap-subset-in-range.md): Generates a sub-bitmap of the source bitmap within a specified range.
      - [BITMAP_SUBSET_LIMIT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/bitmap-subset-limit.md): Generates a sub-bitmap of the source bitmap, beginning with a range from the start value, with a size limit.
      - [BITMAP_TO_ARRAY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/bitmap-array.md): Converts a Bitmap into an Array.
      - [BITMAP_UNION](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/bitmap-union.md): Counts the number of bits set to 1 in the bitmap by performing a logical UNION operation.
      - [BITMAP_XOR](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/bitmap-xor.md): Performs a bitwise XOR (exclusive OR) operation on the two bitmaps.
      - [BITMAP_XOR_COUNT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/bitmap-xor-count.md): Counts the number of bits set to 1 in the bitmap by performing a logical XOR (exclusive OR) operation.
      - [Bitmap Functions](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/bitmap-functions.md): This page provides a comprehensive overview of Bitmap functions in TiDB Cloud Lake, organized by functionality for easy reference.
      - [INTERSECT_COUNT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/intersect-count.md): Counts the number of intersecting bits between two bitmap columns.
      - [SUB_BITMAP](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/sub-bitmap.md): Generates a sub-bitmap of the source bitmap, beginning from the start index, with a specified size.
    - Conversion Functions
      - [BUILD_BITMAP](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/build-bitmap.md): Converts an array of positive integers to a BITMAP value.
      - [CAST::](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/cast.md): Converts a value from one data type to another. is an alias for CAST.
      - [Conversion Functions](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/conversion-functions.md): This page provides a comprehensive overview of Conversion functions in TiDB Cloud Lake, organized by functionality for easy reference.
      - [TO_BINARY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-binary.md): Converts supported data types, including string, variant, bitmap, geometry, and geography, into their binary representation (hex format).
      - [TO_BITMAP](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-bitmap.md): Converts a value to BITMAP data type.
      - [TO_BOOLEAN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-boolean.md): Converts a value to BOOLEAN data type.
      - [TO_DECIMAL](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-decimal.md): Converts a value to DECIMAL data type.
      - [TO_FLOAT32](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-float32.md): Converts a value to FLOAT32 data type.
      - [TO_FLOAT64](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-float64.md): Converts a value to FLOAT64 data type.
      - [TO_HEX](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-hex.md): For a string argument str, TO_HEX() returns a hexadecimal string representation of str where each byte of each character in str is converted to two hexadecimal digits. The inverse of this operation is performed by the UNHEX() function.
      - [TO_INT16](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-int16.md): Converts a value to INT16 data type.
      - [TO_INT32](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-int32.md): Converts a value to INT32 data type.
      - [TO_INT64](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-int64.md): Converts a value to INT64 data type.
      - [TO_INT8](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-int8.md): Converts a value to INT8 data type.
      - [TO_STRING](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-string.md): Converts a value to String data type, or converts a Date value to a specific string format. To customize the format of date and time in TiDB Cloud Lake, you can utilize specifiers. These specifiers allow you to define the desired format for date and time values. For a comprehensive list of supported specifiers, see Formatting Date and Time.
      - [TO_TEXT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-text.md): Alias for TO_STRING.
      - [TO_UINT16](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-uint16.md): Converts a value to UINT16 data type.
      - [TO_UINT32](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-uint32.md): Converts a value to UINT32 data type.
      - [TO_UINT64](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-uint64.md): Converts a value to UINT64 data type.
      - [TO_UINT8](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-uint8.md): Converts a value to UINT8 data type.
      - [TO_VARCHAR](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-varchar.md): Alias for TO_STRING.
      - [TO_VARIANT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-variant.md): Converts a value to VARIANT data type.
      - [TRY_CAST](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/try-cast.md): Converts a value from one data type to another. Returns NULL on error.
      - [TRY_TO_BINARY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/try-to-binary.md): An enhanced version of TO_BINARY that converts an input expression to a binary value, returning NULL if the conversion fails instead of raising an error.
    - Conditional Functions
      - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/conditional-functions.md): This page provides a comprehensive overview of Conditional functions in TiDB Cloud Lake, organized by functionality for easy reference.
      - [[ NOT ] BETWEEN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/between.md): Returns true if the given numeric or string <expr> falls inside the defined lower and upper limits.
      - [CASE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/case.md): Handles IF/THEN logic. It is structured with at least one pair of WHEN and THEN statements. Every CASE statement must be concluded with the END keyword. The ELSE statement is optional, providing a way to capture values not explicitly specified in the WHEN and THEN statements.
      - [COALESCE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/coalesce.md): Returns the first non-NULL expression within its arguments; if all arguments are NULL, it returns NULL.
      - [DECODE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/decode.md): The DECODE function compares the select expression to each search expression in order. As soon as a search expression matches the selection expression, the corresponding result expression is returned. If no match is found and a default value is provided, the default value is returned.
      - [ERROR_OR](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/error-or.md): Returns the first non-error expression among its inputs. If all expressions result in errors, it returns NULL.
      - [GREATEST](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/greatest.md): Returns the maximum value from a set of values. If any value in the set is NULL, the function returns NULL.
      - [GREATEST_IGNORE_NULLS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/greatest-ignore-nulls.md): Returns the maximum value from a set of values, ignoring any NULL values.
      - [IF](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/if.md): If <cond1> is TRUE, it returns <expr1>. Otherwise if <cond2> is TRUE, it returns <expr2>, and so on.
      - [IFF](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/iff.md): Alias for IF.
      - [IFNULL](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/ifnull.md): If <expr1> is NULL, returns <expr2>, otherwise returns <expr1>.
      - [[ NOT ] IN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/in.md): Checks whether a value is (or is not) in an explicit list.
      - [IS [ NOT ] DISTINCT FROM](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/is-distinct-from.md): Compares whether two expressions are equal (or not equal) with awareness of nullability, meaning it treats NULLs as known values for comparing equality.
      - [IS_ERROR](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/is-error.md): Returns a Boolean value indicating whether an expression is an error value.
      - [IS_NOT_ERROR](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/is-not-error.md): Returns a Boolean value indicating whether an expression is an error value.
      - [IS_NOT_NULL](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/is-not-null.md): Checks whether a value is not NULL.
      - [IS_NULL](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/is-null.md): Checks whether a value is NULL.
      - [LEAST](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/least.md): Returns the minimum value from a set of values. If any value in the set is NULL, the function returns NULL.
      - [LEAST_IGNORE_NULLS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/least-ignore-nulls.md): Returns the maximum value from a set of values, ignoring any NULL values.
      - [NULLIF](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/nullif.md): Returns NULL if two expressions are equal. Otherwise return expr1. They must have the same data type.
      - [NVL](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/nvl.md): If <expr1> is NULL, returns <expr2>, otherwise returns <expr1>.
      - [NVL2](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/nvl2.md): Returns <expr2> if <expr1> is not NULL; otherwise, it returns <expr3>.
    - Numeric Functions
      - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/numeric-functions.md): This page provides a comprehensive overview of Numeric functions in TiDB Cloud Lake, organized by functionality for easy reference.
      - [ABS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/abs.md): Returns the absolute value of x.
      - [ACOS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/acos.md): Returns the arc cosine of x, that is, the value whose cosine is x. Returns NULL if x is not in the range -1 to 1.
      - [ADD](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/add.md): Alias for PLUS.
      - [ASIN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/asin.md): Returns the arc sine of x, that is, the value whose sine is x. Returns NULL if x is not in the range -1 to 1.
      - [ATAN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/atan.md): Returns the arc tangent of x, that is, the value whose tangent is x.
      - [ATAN2](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/atan-sql.md): Returns the arc tangent of the two variables x and y. It is similar to calculating the arc tangent of y / x, except that the signs of both arguments are used to determine the quadrant of the result. ATAN(y, x) is a synonym for ATAN2(y, x).
      - [CBRT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/cbrt.md): Returns the cube root of a nonnegative number x.
      - [CEIL](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/ceil.md): Rounds the number up.
      - [CEILING](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/ceiling.md): Alias for CEIL.
      - [COS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/cos.md): Returns the cosine of x, where x is given in radians.
      - [COT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/cot.md): Returns the cotangent of x, where x is given in radians.
      - [CRC32](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/crc.md): Returns the CRC32 checksum of x, where 'x' is expected to be a string and (if possible) is treated as one if it is not.
      - [DEGREES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/degrees.md): Returns the argument x, converted from radians to degrees, where x is given in radians.
      - [DIV](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/div.md): Returns the quotient by dividing the first number by the second one, rounding down to the closest smaller integer. Equivalent to the division operator //.
      - [DIV0](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/div0.md): Returns the quotient by dividing the first number by the second one. Returns 0 if the second number is 0.
      - [DIVNULL](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/divnull.md): Returns the quotient by dividing the first number by the second one. Returns NULL if the second number is 0 or NULL.
      - [EXP](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/exp.md): Returns the value of e (the base of natural logarithms) raised to the power of x.
      - [FACTORIAL](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/factorial.md): Returns the factorial logarithm of x. If x is less than or equal to 0, the function returns 0.
      - [FLOOR](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/floor.md): Rounds the number down.
      - [INTDIV](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/intdiv.md): Alias for DIV.
      - [LN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/ln.md): Returns the natural logarithm of x; that is, the base-e logarithm of x. If x is less than or equal to 0.0E0, the function returns NULL.
      - [LOG10](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/log.md): Returns the base-10 logarithm of x. If x is less than or equal to 0.0E0, the function returns NULL.
      - [LOG2](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/log-sql.md): Returns the base-2 logarithm of x. If x is less than or equal to 0.0E0, the function returns NULL.
      - [LOG(b, x)](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/log-b-x.md): Returns the base-b logarithm of x. If x is less than or equal to 0.0E0, the function returns NULL.
      - [LOG(x)](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/log-x.md): Returns the natural logarithm of x. If x is less than or equal to 0.0E0, the function returns NULL.
      - [MINUS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/minus.md): Negates a numeric value.
      - [MOD](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/mod.md): Alias for MODULO.
      - [MODULO](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/modulo.md): Returns the remainder of x divided by y. If y is 0, it returns an error.
      - [MULTIPLY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/multiply.md): The MULTIPLY function performs multiplication between two numbers. It is equivalent to using the * operator.
      - [NEG](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/neg.md): Alias for MINUS.
      - [NEGATE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/negate.md): Alias for MINUS.
      - [PI](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/pi.md): Returns the value of π as a floating-point value.
      - [PLUS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/plus.md): Calculates the sum of two numeric or decimal values.
      - [POW](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/pow.md): Returns the value of x to the power of y.
      - [POWER](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/power.md): Alias for POW.
      - [RADIANS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/radians.md): Returns the argument x, converted from degrees to radians.
      - [RAND()](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/rand.md): Returns a random floating-point value v in the range 0 <= v < 1.0. To obtain a random integer R in the range i <= R < j, use the expression FLOOR(i + RAND() * (j − i)).
      - [RAND(n)](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/rand-n.md): Returns a random floating-point value v in the range 0 <= v < 1.0. To obtain a random integer R in the range i <= R < j, use the expression FLOOR(i + RAND() * (j − i)). Argument n is used as the seed value. For equal argument values, RAND(n) returns the same value each time, and thus produces a repeatable sequence of column values.
      - [ROUND](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/round.md): Rounds the argument x to d decimal places. The rounding algorithm depends on the data type of x. d defaults to 0 if not specified. d can be negative to cause d digits left of the decimal point of the value x to become zero. The maximum absolute value for d is 30; any digits in excess of 30 (or -30) are truncated.
      - [SIGN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/sign.md): Returns the sign of the argument as -1, 0, or 1, depending on whether x is negative, zero, or positive or NULL if the argument was NULL.
      - [SIN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/sin.md): Returns the sine of x, where x is given in radians.
      - [SQRT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/sqrt.md): Returns the square root of a nonnegative number x. Returns Nan for negative input.
      - [SUBTRACT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/subtract.md): Alias for MINUS.
      - [TAN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/tan.md): Returns the tangent of x, where x is given in radians.
      - [TRUNC](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/trunc.md): Returns the number x, truncated to d decimal places. If d is 0, the result has no decimal point or fractional part. d can be negative to cause d digits left of the decimal point of the value x to become zero. The maximum absolute value for d is 30; any digits in excess of 30 (or -30) are truncated.
      - [TRUNCATE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/truncate.md): Returns the number x, truncated to d decimal places. If d is 0, the result has no decimal point or fractional part. d can be negative to cause d digits left of the decimal point of the value x to become zero. The maximum absolute value for d is 30; any digits in excess of 30 (or -30) are truncated.
    - Date & Time Functions
      - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/date-time-functions.md): This page provides a comprehensive overview of Date & Time functions in TiDB Cloud Lake, organized by functionality for easy reference.
      - [ADD_MONTHS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/add-months.md): The add_months() function adds a specified number of months to a given date or timestamp.
      - [ADD TIME INTERVAL](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/add-interval.md): Add a time interval to a date or timestamp, return the result of date or timestamp type.
      - [AGE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/age.md): The age() function calculates the difference between two timestamps or the difference between a timestamp and the current date and time.
      - [CONVERT_TIMEZONE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/convert-timezone.md): Converts a timestamp from one timezone to another and requires a valid IANA destination timezone name.
      - [CURRENT_TIMESTAMP](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/current-timestamp.md): Alias for NOW.
      - [DATE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/date.md): Alias for TO_DATE.
      - [DATE_ADD](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/date-add.md): Adds a specified time interval to a DATE or TIMESTAMP value.
      - [DATE_BETWEEN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/date-between.md): Calculates the time interval between two dates or timestamps, returning the difference as an integer in the specified unit, with positive values indicating the first time is earlier than the second, and negative values indicating the opposite.
      - [DATE_DIFF](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/date-diff.md): Calculates the difference between two dates or timestamps based on a specified time unit. The result is positive if the <end_date> is after the <start_date>, and negative if it's before.
      - [DATE_FORMAT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/date-format.md): Alias for TO_STRING.
      - [DATE_PART](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/date-part.md): Retrieves the designated portion of a date or timestamp.
      - [DATE_SUB](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/date-sub.md): Subtract the time interval or date interval from the provided date or date with time (timestamp/datetime).
      - [DATE_TRUNC](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/date-trunc.md): Truncates a date or timestamp to a specified precision, providing a standardized way to manipulate dates and timestamps. This function is designed to be compatible with various database systems, making it easier for users to migrate and work with different databases.
      - [DAY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/day.md): Alias for TO_DAY_OF_MONTH.
      - [EXTRACT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/extract.md): Retrieves the designated portion of a date, timestamp, or interval.
      - [LAST_DAY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/last-day.md): Returns the last day of the specified interval (week, month, quarter, or year) based on the provided date or timestamp.
      - [MILLENNIUM](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/millennium.md): Returns the millennium of a given date or timestamp. The 1st millennium spans years 0001–1000, the 2nd spans 1001–2000, the 3rd spans 2001–3000, and so on.
      - [MONTH](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/month.md): Alias for TO_MONTH.
      - [MONTHS_BETWEEN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/months-between.md): Returns the number of months between *date1* and *date2*.
      - [NEXT_DAY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/next-day.md): Returns the date of the upcoming specified day of the week after the given date or timestamp.
      - [NOW](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/now.md): Returns the current date and time.
      - [PREVIOUS_DAY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/previous-day.md): Returns the date of the most recent specified day of the week before the given date or timestamp.
      - [QUARTER](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/quarter.md): Alias for TO_QUARTER.
      - [STR_TO_DATE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/str-to-date.md): Alias for TO_DATE.
      - [STR_TO_TIMESTAMP](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/str-to-timestamp.md): Alias for TO_TIMESTAMP.
      - [SUBTRACT TIME INTERVAL](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/subtract-interval.md): Subtract time interval function.
      - [TIME_SLICE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/time-slice.md): TIME_SLICE is a scalar function used to map a single date/timestamp value to a fixed calendar interval (slice or bucket).
      - [TIME_SLOT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/time-slot.md): Rounds the time to the half-hour. ## Syntax.
      - [TIMESTAMP_DIFF](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/timestamp-diff.md): Calculates the difference between two timestamps and returns the result as an INTERVAL.
      - [TIMEZONE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/timezone.md): Returns the timezone for the current connection.
      - [TO_DATE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-date.md): Converts an expression to a date, including.
      - [TO_DATETIME](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/datetime.md): Alias for TO_TIMESTAMP.
      - [TO_DAY_OF_MONTH](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-day-of-month.md): Convert a date or date with time (timestamp/datetime) to a UInt8 number containing the number of the day of the month (1-31).
      - [TO_DAY_OF_WEEK](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/day-week.md): Converts a date or date with time (timestamp/datetime) to a UInt8 number containing the number of the day of the week (Monday is 1, and Sunday is 7).
      - [TO_DAY_OF_YEAR](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/day-year.md): Convert a date or date with time (timestamp/datetime) to a UInt16 number containing the number of the day of the year (1-366).
      - [TO_HOUR](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/hour.md): Converts a date with time (timestamp/datetime) to a UInt8 number containing the number of the hour in 24-hour time (0-23). This function assumes that if clocks are moved ahead, it is by one hour and occurs at 2 a.m., and if clocks are moved back, it is by one hour and occurs at 3 a.m. (which is not always true – even in Moscow the clocks were twice changed at a different time).
      - [TO_MINUTE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/minute.md): Converts a date with time (timestamp/datetime) to a UInt8 number containing the number of the minute of the hour (0-59).
      - [TO_MONDAY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/monday.md): Round down a date or date with time (timestamp/datetime) to the nearest Monday. Returns the date.
      - [TO_MONTH](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-month.md): Convert a date or date with time (timestamp/datetime) to a UInt8 number containing the month number (1-12).
      - [TO_QUARTER](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-quarter.md): Retrieves the quarter (1, 2, 3, or 4) from a given date or timestamp.
      - [TO_SECOND](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/second.md): Converts a date with time (timestamp/datetime) to a UInt8 number containing the number of the second in the minute (0-59).
      - [TO_START_OF_DAY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-start-of-day.md): Rounds down a date with time (timestamp/datetime) to the start of the day. ## Syntax.
      - [TO_START_OF_FIFTEEN_MINUTES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/start-fifteen-minutes.md): Rounds down the date with time (timestamp/datetime) to the start of the fifteen-minute interval. ## Syntax.
      - [TO_START_OF_FIVE_MINUTES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/start-five-minutes.md): Rounds down a date with time (timestamp/datetime) to the start of the five-minute interval. ## Syntax.
      - [TO_START_OF_HOUR](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-start-of-hour.md): Rounds down a date with time (timestamp/datetime) to the start of the hour. ## Syntax.
      - [TO_START_OF_ISO_YEAR](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/start-iso-year.md): Returns the first day of the ISO year for a date or a date with time (timestamp/datetime).
      - [TO_START_OF_MINUTE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-start-of-minute.md): Rounds down a date with time (timestamp/datetime) to the start of the minute.
      - [TO_START_OF_MONTH](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-start-of-month.md): Rounds down a date or date with time (timestamp/datetime) to the first day of the month. Returns the date.
      - [TO_START_OF_QUARTER](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-start-of-quarter.md): Rounds down a date or date with time (timestamp/datetime) to the first day of the quarter. The first day of the quarter is either 1 January, 1 April, 1 July, or 1 October. Returns the date.
      - [TO_START_OF_SECOND](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-start-of-second.md): Rounds down a date with time (timestamp/datetime) to the start of the second.
      - [TO_START_OF_TEN_MINUTES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/start-ten-minutes.md): Rounds down a date with time (timestamp/datetime) to the start of the ten-minute interval.
      - [TO_START_OF_WEEK](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-start-of-week.md): Returns the first day of the week for a date or a date with time (timestamp/datetime). The first day of a week can be Sunday or Monday, which is specified by the argument mode.
      - [TO_START_OF_YEAR](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-start-of-year.md): Returns the first day of the year for a date or a date with time (timestamp/datetime).
      - [TO_TIMESTAMP](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-timestamp.md): Converts an expression to a date with time.
      - [TO_TIMESTAMP_TZ](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/timestamp-tz.md): Converts a value to TIMESTAMP_TZ, keeping both the UTC moment and the timezone offset. Use TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP_TZ if you prefer NULL instead of an error.
      - [TO_UNIX_TIMESTAMP](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/unix-timestamp.md): Converts a timestamp in a date/time format to a Unix timestamp format. A Unix timestamp represents the number of seconds that have elapsed since January 1, 1970, at 000000 UTC.
      - [TO_WEEK_OF_YEAR](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-week-of-year.md): Calculates the week number within a year for a given date.
      - [TO_YEAR](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-year.md): Converts a date or date with time (timestamp/datetime) to a UInt16 number containing the year number (AD).
      - [TO_YYYYMM](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/yyyymm.md): Converts a date or date with time (timestamp/datetime) to a UInt32 number containing the year and month number.
      - [TO_YYYYMMDD](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/yyyymmdd.md): Converts a date or date with time (timestamp/datetime) to a UInt32 number containing the year and month number (YYYY * 10000 + MM * 100 + DD). ## Syntax.
      - [TO_YYYYMMDDHH](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/yyyymmddhh.md): Formats a given date or timestamp into a string representation in the format "YYYYMMDDHH" (Year, Month, Day, Hour).
      - [TO_YYYYMMDDHHMMSS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/yyyymmddhhmmss.md): Convert a date or date with time (timestamp/datetime) to a UInt64 number containing the year and month number (YYYY * 10000000000 + MM * 100000000 + DD * 1000000 + hh * 10000 + mm * 100 + ss).
      - [TODAY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/today.md): Returns current date.
      - [TOMORROW](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/tomorrow.md): Returns tomorrow date, same as today() + 1.
      - [TRUNC](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/trunc-sql.md): Truncates a date or timestamp to a specified precision. This function follows a widely adopted date truncation syntax, making it easier for users migrating from other database systems.
      - [TRY_TO_DATETIME](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/try-to-datetime.md): Alias for TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP.
      - [TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/try-to-timestamp.md): A variant of TO_TIMESTAMP in TiDB Cloud Lake that, while performing the same conversion of an input expression to a timestamp, incorporates error-handling support by returning NULL if the conversion fails instead of raising an error.
      - [WEEK](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/week.md): Alias for TO_WEEK_OF_YEAR.
      - [WEEKOFYEAR](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/weekofyear.md): Alias for TO_WEEK_OF_YEAR.
      - [YEAR](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/year.md): Alias for TO_YEAR.
      - [YEARWEEK](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/yearweek.md): Returns the year and week number in YYYYWW format, according to ISO week date. Week 1 is the week with the first Thursday of the year.
      - [YESTERDAY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/yesterday.md): Returns yesterday date, same as today() - 1.
    - Interval Functions
      - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/interval-functions.md): This section provides reference information for the interval functions in TiDB Cloud Lake. Interval functions allow you to create interval values of various time units for use in date and time calculations.
      - [EPOCH](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/epoch.md): Alias for TO_SECONDS.
      - [TO_CENTURIES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-centuries.md): Converts a specified number of centuries into an Interval type.
      - [TO_DAYS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/days.md): Converts a specified number of days into an Interval type.
      - [TO_DECADES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/decades.md): Converts a specified number of decades into an Interval type.
      - [TO_HOURS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/hours.md): Converts a specified number of hours into an Interval type.
      - [TO_MICROSECONDS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/microseconds.md): Converts a specified number of microseconds into an Interval type.
      - [TO_MILLENNIA](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/millennia.md): Converts a specified number of millennia into an Interval type.
      - [TO_MILLISECONDS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/milliseconds.md): Converts a specified number of milliseconds into an Interval type.
      - [TO_MINUTES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/minutes.md): Converts a specified number of minutes into an Interval type.
      - [TO_MONTHS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/months.md): Converts a specified number of months into an Interval type.
      - [TO_SECONDS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/seconds.md): Converts a specified number of seconds into an Interval type.
      - [TO_WEEKS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/weeks.md): Converts a specified number of weeks into an Interval type.
      - [TO_YEARS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/years.md): Converts a specified number of years into an Interval type.
    - String Functions
      - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/string-functions-overview.md): This page provides a comprehensive overview of String functions in TiDB Cloud Lake, organized by functionality for easy reference.
      - [ASCII](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/ascii.md): Returns the numeric value of the leftmost character of the string str.
      - [BIN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/bin.md): Returns a string representation of the binary value of N.
      - [BIT_LENGTH](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/bit-length.md): Return the length of a string in bits.
      - [CHAR](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/char.md): Returns the character(s) for each integer passed. The function converts each integer to its corresponding Unicode character.
      - [CHAR_LENGTH](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/char-length.md): Alias for LENGTH.
      - [CHARACTER_LENGTH](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/character-length.md): Alias for LENGTH.
      - [CONCAT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/concat.md): Returns the string that results from concatenating the arguments. May have one or more arguments. If all arguments are nonbinary strings, the result is a nonbinary string. If the arguments include any binary strings, the result is a binary string. A numeric argument is converted to its equivalent nonbinary string form.
      - [CONCAT_WS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/concat-ws.md): CONCAT_WS() stands for Concatenate With Separator and is a special form of CONCAT(). The first argument is the separator for the rest of the arguments. The separator is added between the strings to be concatenated. The separator can be a string, as can the rest of the arguments. If the separator is NULL, the result is NULL.
      - [FROM_BASE64](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/from-base64.md): Takes a string encoded with the base-64 encoded rules and returns the decoded result as a binary. The result is NULL if the argument is NULL or not a valid base-64 string.
      - [FROM_HEX](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/from-hex.md): Alias for UNHEX.
      - [GLOB](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/glob.md): Performs case-sensitive pattern matching using wildcard characters.
      - [HEX](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/hex.md): Alias for TO_HEX.
      - [INSERT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/insert-sql.md): Returns the string str, with the substring beginning at position pos and len characters long replaced by the string newstr. Returns the original string if pos is not within the length of the string. Replaces the rest of the string from position pos if len is not within the length of the rest of the string. Returns NULL if any argument is NULL.
      - [INSTR](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/instr.md): Returns the position of the first occurrence of substring substr in string str. This is the same as the two-argument form of LOCATE(), except that the order of the arguments is reversed.
      - [JARO_WINKLER](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/jaro-winkler.md): Calculates the Jaro-Winkler distance between two strings. It is commonly used for measuring the similarity between strings, with values ranging from 0.0 (completely dissimilar) to 1.0 (identical strings).
      - [LCASE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/lcase.md): Alias for LOWER.
      - [LEFT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/left.md): Returns the leftmost len characters from the string str, or NULL if any argument is NULL. If len is greater than the length of str, the entire str is returned.
      - [LENGTH](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/length.md): Returns the length of a given input string or binary value. In the case of strings, the length represents the count of characters, with each UTF-8 character considered as a single character. For binary data, the length corresponds to the number of bytes.
      - [LENGTH_UTF8](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/length-utf8.md): Alias for LENGTH.
      - [LIKE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/like.md): Pattern matching using an SQL pattern. Returns 1 (TRUE) or 0 (FALSE). If either expr or pat is NULL, the result is NULL.
      - [LOCATE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/locate.md): The first syntax returns the position of the first occurrence of substring substr in string str. The second syntax returns the position of the first occurrence of substring substr in string str, starting at position pos. Returns 0 if substr is not in str. Returns NULL if any argument is NULL.
      - [LOWER](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/lower.md): Returns a string with all characters changed to lowercase.
      - [LPAD](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/lpad.md): Returns the string str, left-padded with the string padstr to a length of len characters. If str is longer than len, the return value is shortened to len characters.
      - [LTRIM](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/ltrim.md): Removes all occurrences of any character present in the specified trim string from the left side of the string.
      - [MID](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/mid.md): Alias for SUBSTR.
      - [NOT LIKE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/not-like.md): Pattern not matching using an SQL pattern. Returns 1 (TRUE) or 0 (FALSE). If either expr or pat is NULL, the result is NULL.
      - [NOT REGEXP](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/not-regexp.md): Returns 1 if the string expr doesn't match the regular expression specified by the pattern pat, 0 otherwise.
      - [NOT RLIKE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/not-rlike.md): Returns 1 if the string expr doesn't match the regular expression specified by the pattern pat, 0 otherwise.
      - [OCT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/oct.md): Returns a string representation of the octal value of N.
      - [OCTET_LENGTH](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/octet-length.md): OCTET_LENGTH() is a synonym for LENGTH().
      - [ORD](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/ord.md): If the leftmost character is not a multibyte character, ORD() returns the same value as the ASCII() function.
      - [POSITION](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/position.md): POSITION(substr IN str) is a synonym for LOCATE(substr,str). Returns the position of the first occurrence of substring substr in string str. Returns 0 if substr is not in str. Returns NULL if any argument is NULL.
      - [QUOTE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/quote.md): Quotes a string to produce a result that can be used as a properly escaped data value in an SQL statement.
      - [REGEXP](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/regexp.md): Returns true if the string <expr> matches the regular expression specified by the <pattern>, false otherwise.
      - [REGEXP_INSTR](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/regexp-instr.md): Returns the starting index of the substring of the string expr that matches the regular expression specified by the pattern pat, 0 if there is no match. If expr or pat is NULL, the return value is NULL. Character indexes begin at 1.
      - [REGEXP_LIKE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/regexp-like.md): REGEXP_LIKE function is used to check that whether the string matches regular expression.
      - [REGEXP_REPLACE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/regexp-replace.md): Replaces occurrences in the string expr that match the regular expression specified by the pattern pat with the replacement string repl, and returns the resulting string. If expr, pat, or repl is NULL, the return value is NULL.
      - [REGEXP_SPLIT_TO_ARRAY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/regexp-split-array.md): Splits a string using a regular expression pattern and returns the segments as an array.
      - [REGEXP_SPLIT_TO_TABLE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/regexp-split-table.md): Splits a string using a regular expression pattern and returns each segment as a table.
      - [REGEXP_SUBSTR](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/regexp-substr.md): Returns the substring of the string expr that matches the regular expression specified by the pattern pat, NULL if there is no match. If expr or pat is NULL, the return value is NULL.
      - [REPEAT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/repeat.md): Returns a string consisting of the string str repeated count times. If count is less than 1, returns an empty string. Returns NULL if str or count are NULL.
      - [REPLACE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/replace-sql.md): Returns the string str with all occurrences of the string from_str replaced by the string to_str.
      - [REVERSE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/reverse.md): Returns the string str with the order of the characters reversed.
      - [RIGHT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/right.md): Returns the rightmost len characters from the string str, or NULL if any argument is NULL.
      - [RLIKE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/rlike.md): Alias for REGEXP.
      - [RPAD](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/rpad.md): Returns the string str, right-padded with the string padstr to a length of len characters. If str is longer than len, the return value is shortened to len characters.
      - [RTRIM](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/rtrim.md): Removes all occurrences of any character present in the specified trim string from the right side of the string.
      - [SOUNDEX](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/soundex.md): Generates the Soundex code for a string.
      - [SOUNDS LIKE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/sounds-like.md): Compares the pronunciation of two strings by their Soundex codes. Soundex is a phonetic algorithm that produces a code representing the pronunciation of a string, allowing for approximate matching of strings based on their pronunciation rather than their spelling. TiDB Cloud Lake offers the SOUNDEX function that allows you to get the Soundex code from a string.
      - [SPACE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/space.md): Returns a string consisting of N blank space characters.
      - [SPLIT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/split.md): Splits a string using a specified delimiter and returns the resulting parts as an array.
      - [SPLIT_PART](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/split-part.md): Splits a string using a specified delimiter and returns the specified part.
      - [STRCMP](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/strcmp.md): Returns 0 if the strings are the same, -1 if the first argument is smaller than the second, and 1 otherwise.
      - [SUBSTR](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/substr.md): Extracts a string containing a specific number of characters from a particular position of a given string.
      - [SUBSTRING](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/substring.md): Alias for SUBSTR.
      - [TO_BASE64](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-base64.md): Converts the string argument to base-64 encoded form and returns the result as a character string. If the argument is not a string, it is converted to a string before conversion takes place. The result is NULL if the argument is NULL.
      - [TRANSLATE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/translate.md): Transforms a given string by replacing specific characters with corresponding replacements, as defined by the provided mapping.
      - [TRIM](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/trim.md): Removes spaces, specific characters, or substrings from the start, end, or both sides of a string.
      - [TRIM_BOTH](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/trim-both.md): Removes all occurrences of the specified trim string from the beginning, end, or both sides of the string.
      - [TRIM_LEADING](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/trim-leading.md): Removes all occurrences of the specified trim string from the beginning of the string.
      - [TRIM_TRAILING](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/trim-trailing.md): Removes all occurrences of the specified trim string from the end of the string.
      - [UCASE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/ucase.md): Alias for UPPER.
      - [UNHEX](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/unhex.md): For a string argument str, UNHEX(str) interprets each pair of characters in the argument as a hexadecimal number and converts it to the byte represented by the number. The return value is a binary string.
      - [UPPER](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/upper.md): Returns a string with all characters changed to uppercase.
    - Aggregate Functions
      - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/aggregate-functions.md): This page provides a comprehensive overview of aggregate functions in TiDB Cloud Lake, organized by functionality for easy reference.
      - [ANY_VALUE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/any-value.md): Aggregate function.
      - [APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/approx-count-distinct.md): Estimates the number of distinct values in a data set with the HyperLogLog algorithm.
      - [ARG_MAX](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/arg-max.md): Calculates the arg value for a maximum val value. If there are several values of arg for maximum values of val, returns the first of these values encountered.
      - [ARG_MIN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/arg-min.md): Calculates the arg value for a minimum val value. If there are several different values of arg for minimum values of val, returns the first of these values encountered.
      - [ARRAY_AGG](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-agg.md): The ARRAY_AGG function (also known by its alias LIST) transforms all the values, excluding NULL, of a specific column in a query result into an array.
      - [AVG](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/avg.md): Aggregate function.
      - [AVG_IF](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/avg-if.md): The suffix -If can be appended to the name of any aggregate function. In this case, the aggregate function accepts an extra argument – a condition.
      - [bool_and](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/bool-and.md): Returns true if all input values are true, otherwise false.
      - [bool_or](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/bool-or.md): Returns true if at least one input value is true, otherwise false.
      - [COUNT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/count.md): The COUNT() function returns the number of records returned by a SELECT query.
      - [COUNT_DISTINCT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/count-distinct.md): Aggregate function.
      - [COUNT_IF](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/count-if.md): The suffix _IF can be appended to the name of any aggregate function. In this case, the aggregate function accepts an extra argument – a condition.
      - [COVAR_POP](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/covar-pop.md): Returns the population covariance of a set of number pairs.
      - [COVAR_SAMP](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/covar-samp.md): Returns the sample covariance (Σ((x - x̅)(y - y̅)) / (n - 1)) of two data columns.
      - [GROUP_ARRAY_MOVING_AVG](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/group-array-moving-avg.md): The GROUP_ARRAY_MOVING_AVG function calculates the moving average of input values. The function can take the window size as a parameter. If left unspecified, the function takes the window size equal to the number of input values.
      - [GROUP_ARRAY_MOVING_SUM](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/group-array-moving-sum.md): The GROUP_ARRAY_MOVING_SUM function calculates the moving sum of input values. The function can take the window size as a parameter. If left unspecified, the function takes the window size equal to the number of input values.
      - [GROUP_CONCAT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/group-concat.md): Alias for LISTAGG.
      - [HISTOGRAM](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/histogram.md): Generates a data distribution histogram using an "equal height" bucketing strategy.
      - [JSON_ARRAY_AGG](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/json-array-agg.md): Converts values into a JSON array while skipping NULLs.
      - [JSON_OBJECT_AGG](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/json-object-agg.md): Converts key-value pairs into a JSON object. For each row in the input, it generates a key-value pair where the key is derived from the <key_expression> and the value is derived from the <value_expression>. These key-value pairs are then combined into a single JSON object.
      - [KURTOSIS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/kurtosis.md): Aggregate function.
      - [LISTAGG](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/listagg.md): Concatenates values from multiple rows into a single string, separated by a specified delimiter. This operation can be performed using two different function types - Aggregate Function The concatenation happens across all rows in the entire result set. - Window Function The concatenation happens within each partition of the result set, as defined by the PARTITION BY clause.
      - [MARKOV_TRAIN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/markov-train.md): Extracting patterns from datasets using Markov models.
      - [MAX](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/max.md): Aggregate function.
      - [MAX_IF](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/max-if.md): The suffix _IF can be appended to the name of any aggregate function. In this case, the aggregate function accepts an extra argument – a condition.
      - [MEDIAN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/median.md): The MEDIAN() function.
      - [MEDIAN_TDIGEST](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/median-tdigest.md): Computes the median of a numeric data sequence using the t-digest algorithm.
      - [MIN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/min.md): Aggregate function.
      - [MIN_IF](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/min-if.md): The suffix _IF can be appended to the name of any aggregate function. In this case, the aggregate function accepts an extra argument – a condition.
      - [MODE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/mode.md): Returns the value that appears most frequently in a group of values.
      - [QUANTILE_CONT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/quantile-cont.md): The QUANTILE_CONT() function computes the interpolated quantile number of a numeric data sequence.
      - [QUANTILE_DISC](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/quantile-disc.md): The QUANTILE_DISC() function computes the exact quantile number of a numeric data sequence.
      - [QUANTILE_TDIGEST](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/quantile-tdigest.md): Computes an approximate quantile of a numeric data sequence using the t-digest algorithm.
      - [QUANTILE_TDIGEST_WEIGHTED](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/quantile-tdigest-weighted.md): Computes an approximate quantile of a numeric data sequence using the t-digest algorithm. This function takes into account the weight of each sequence member. Memory consumption is log(n), where n is a number of values.
      - [RETENTION](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/retention.md): Aggregate function.
      - [SKEWNESS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/skewness.md): Aggregate function.
      - [ST_COLLECT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-collect.md): Collects multiple GEOMETRY values into a single GEOMETRY result.
      - [ST_ENVELOPE_AGG](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-envelope-agg.md): Aggregates multiple GEOMETRY values and returns the minimum bounding rectangle that covers all non-NULL inputs.
      - [ST_INTERSECTION_AGG](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-intersection-agg.md): Aggregates multiple GEOMETRY values by repeatedly applying ST_INTERSECTION and returns the common overlapping part.
      - [ST_UNION_AGG](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-union-agg.md): Aggregates multiple GEOMETRY values by repeatedly applying ST_UNION and returns the merged GEOMETRY result.
      - [STDDEV_POP](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/stddev-pop.md): Aggregate function.
      - [STDDEV_SAMP](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/stddev-samp.md): Returns the sample standard deviation (the square root of VAR_SAMP()) of an expression.
      - [STRING_AGG](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/string-agg.md): Alias for LISTAGG.
      - [SUM](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/sum.md): Calculates the sum of a set of values.
      - [SUM_IF](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/sum-if.md): The suffix -If can be appended to the name of any aggregate function. In this case, the aggregate function accepts an extra argument – a condition.
      - [VAR_POP](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/var-pop.md): Alias for COVAR_POP.
      - [VAR_SAMP](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/var-samp.md): Alias for COVAR_SAMP.
      - [VARIANCE_POP](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/variance-pop.md): Alias for COVAR_POP.
      - [VARIANCE_SAMP](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/variance-samp.md): Alias for COVAR_SAMP.
      - [WINDOW_FUNNEL](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/window-funnel.md): Funnel Analysis.
    - Window Functions
      - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/window-functions-overview.md): Window functions perform calculations across a set of related rows while returning one result per input row. Unlike aggregate functions, window functions don't collapse rows into a single output.
      - [CUME_DIST](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/cume-dist.md): Calculates the cumulative distribution of each row's value. Returns the fraction of rows with values less than or equal to the current row's value.
      - [DENSE_RANK](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/dense-rank.md): Assigns a rank to each row within a partition. Rows with equal values receive the same rank, with no gaps in subsequent rankings.
      - [FIRST](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/first.md): Alias for FIRST_VALUE.
      - [FIRST_VALUE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/first-value.md): Returns the first value in the window frame.
      - [LAG](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/lag.md): Returns the value from a previous row in the result set.
      - [LAST](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/last.md): Alias for LAST_VALUE.
      - [LAST_VALUE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/last-value.md): Returns the last value in the window frame.
      - [LEAD](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/lead.md): Returns the value from a subsequent row in the result set.
      - [NTH_VALUE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/nth-value.md): Returns the value at the specified position (N) within the window frame.
      - [NTILE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/ntile.md): Divides rows into a specified number of buckets and assigns a bucket number to each row. Rows are distributed as evenly as possible across buckets.
      - [PERCENT_RANK](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/percent-rank.md): Calculates the relative rank of each row as a percentage. Returns values between 0 and 1, where 0 represents the lowest rank and 1 represents the highest rank.
      - [RANGE BETWEEN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/range-between.md): Defines a window frame using value-based boundaries for window functions.
      - [RANK](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/rank.md): Assigns a rank to each row within a partition. Rows with equal values receive the same rank, with gaps in subsequent rankings.
      - [ROW_NUMBER](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/row-number.md): Assigns a sequential number to each row within a partition, starting from 1.
      - [ROWS BETWEEN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/rows-between.md): Defines a window frame using row-based boundaries for window functions.
    - Geospatial Functions
      - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/geospatial-functions.md): TiDB Cloud Lake ships with two complementary sets of geospatial capabilities PostGIS-style geometry functions for building and analysing shapes, and H3 utilities for global hexagonal indexing. The tables below group the functions by task so you can quickly locate the right tool, similar to the layout used in the Snowflake documentation.
      - [GEO_DISTANCE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/geo-distance.md): Returns the approximate distance in meters between two points on Earth.
      - [GEO_TO_H3](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/geo-to-h3.md): Returns the H3 index of the hexagon cell where the given location resides. Returning 0 means an error occurred.
      - [GEOHASH_DECODE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/geohash-decode.md): Converts a Geohash-encoded string into latitude/longitude coordinates.
      - [GEOHASH_ENCODE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/geohash-encode.md): Converts a pair of latitude and longitude coordinates into a Geohash-encoded string.
      - [GREAT_CIRCLE_ANGLE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/great-circle-angle.md): Returns the central angle in degrees between two points on a sphere.
      - [GREAT_CIRCLE_DISTANCE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/great-circle-distance.md): Returns the great-circle distance in meters between two points on a sphere.
      - [H3_CELL_AREA_M2](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-cell-area-m2.md): Returns the exact area of specific cell in square meters.
      - [H3_CELL_AREA_RADS2](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-cell-area-rads2.md): Returns the exact area of specific cell in square radians.
      - [H3_DISTANCE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-distance.md): Returns the grid distance between the the given two H3 indexes.
      - [H3_EDGE_ANGLE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-edge-angle.md): Returns the average length of the H3 hexagon edge in grades.
      - [H3_EDGE_LENGTH_KM](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-edge-length-km.md): Returns the average hexagon edge length in kilometers at the given resolution. Excludes pentagons.
      - [H3_EDGE_LENGTH_M](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-edge-length-m.md): Returns the average hexagon edge length in meters at the given resolution. Excludes pentagons.
      - [H3_EXACT_EDGE_LENGTH_KM](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-exact-edge-length-km.md): Computes the length of this directed edge, in kilometers.
      - [H3_EXACT_EDGE_LENGTH_M](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-exact-edge-length-m.md): Computes the length of this directed edge, in meters.
      - [H3_EXACT_EDGE_LENGTH_RADS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-exact-edge-length-rads.md): Computes the length of this directed edge, in radians.
      - [H3_GET_BASE_CELL](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-get-base-cell.md): Returns the base cell number of the given H3 index.
      - [H3_GET_DESTINATION_INDEX_FROM_UNIDIRECTIONAL_EDGE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-get-destination-index-unidirectional-edge.md): Returns the destination hexagon index from the unidirectional edge H3Index.
      - [H3_GET_FACES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-get-faces.md): Finds all icosahedron faces intersected by the given H3 index. Faces are represented as integers from 0-19.
      - [H3_GET_INDEXES_FROM_UNIDIRECTIONAL_EDGE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-get-indexes-unidirectional-edge.md): Returns the origin and destination hexagon indexes from the given unidirectional edge H3Index.
