      - [H3_GET_ORIGIN_INDEX_FROM_UNIDIRECTIONAL_EDGE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-get-origin-index-unidirectional-edge.md): Returns the origin hexagon index from the unidirectional edge H3Index.
      - [H3_GET_RESOLUTION](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-get-resolution.md): Returns the resolution of the given H3 index.
      - [H3_GET_UNIDIRECTIONAL_EDGE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-get-unidirectional-edge.md): Returns the edge between the given two H3 indexes.
      - [H3_GET_UNIDIRECTIONAL_EDGE_BOUNDARY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-get-unidirectional-edge-boundary.md): Returns the coordinates defining the unidirectional edge.
      - [H3_GET_UNIDIRECTIONAL_EDGES_FROM_HEXAGON](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-get-unidirectional-edges-hexagon.md): Returns all of the unidirectional edges from the provided H3Index.
      - [H3_HEX_AREA_KM2](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-hex-area-km2.md): Returns the average hexagon area in square kilometers at the given resolution. Excludes pentagons.
      - [H3_HEX_AREA_M2](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-hex-area-m2.md): Returns the average hexagon area in square meters at the given resolution. Excludes pentagons.
      - [H3_HEX_RING](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-hex-ring.md): Returns the "hollow" ring of hexagons at exactly grid distance k from the given H3 index.
      - [H3_INDEXES_ARE_NEIGHBORS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-indexes-are-neighbors.md): Returns whether or not the provided H3 indexes are neighbors.
      - [H3_IS_PENTAGON](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-is-pentagon.md): Checks if the given H3 index represents a pentagonal cell.
      - [H3_IS_RES_CLASS_III](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-is-res-class-iii.md): Checks if the given H3 index has a resolution with Class III orientation.
      - [H3_IS_VALID](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-is-valid.md): Checks if the given H3 index is valid.
      - [H3_K_RING](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-k-ring.md): Returns an array containing the H3 indexes of the k-ring hexagons surrounding the input H3 index. Each element in this array is an H3 index.
      - [H3_LINE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-line.md): Returns the line of indexes between the given two H3 indexes.
      - [H3_NUM_HEXAGONS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-num-hexagons.md): Returns the number of unique H3 indexes at the given resolution.
      - [H3_TO_CENTER_CHILD](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-to-center-child.md): Returns the center child index at the specified resolution.
      - [H3_TO_CHILDREN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-to-children.md): Returns the indexes contained by h3 at resolution child_res.
      - [H3_TO_GEO](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-to-geo.md): Returns the longitude and latitude corresponding to the given H3 index.
      - [H3_TO_GEO_BOUNDARY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-to-geo-boundary.md): Returns an array containing the longitude and latitude coordinates of the vertices of the hexagon corresponding to the H3 index.
      - [H3_TO_PARENT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-to-parent.md): Returns the parent index containing the h3 at resolution parent_res. Returning 0 means an error occurred.
      - [H3_TO_STRING](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-to-string.md): Converts the representation of the given H3 index to the string representation.
      - [H3_UNIDIRECTIONAL_EDGE_IS_VALID](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/h3-unidirectional-edge-is-valid.md): Determines if the provided H3Index is a valid unidirectional edge index. Returns 1 if it's a unidirectional edge and 0 otherwise.
      - [HAVERSINE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/haversine.md): Calculates the great circle distance in kilometers between two points on the Earth’s surface, using the Haversine formula. The two points are specified by their latitude and longitude in degrees.
      - [POINT_IN_ELLIPSES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/point-in-ellipses.md): Returns 1 if the point lies inside any of the provided ellipses, otherwise returns 0.
      - [POINT_IN_POLYGON](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/point-in-polygon.md): Calculates whether a given point falls within the polygon formed by joining multiple points. A polygon is a closed shape connected by coordinate pairs in the order they appear. Changing the order of coordinate pairs can result in a different shape.
      - [ST_AREA](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-area.md): Returns the area of a GEOMETRY or GEOGRAPHY object. For GEOMETRY inputs, the function uses planar area based on the shoelace formula. For GEOGRAPHY inputs, the function measures geodesic area on an ellipsoidal model of the earth using the method described in Karney (2013).
      - [ST_ASBINARY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-asbinary.md): Alias for ST_ASWKB.
      - [ST_ASEWKB](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-asewkb.md): Converts a GEOMETRY or GEOGRAPHY object into a EWKB(extended well-known-binary) format representation.
      - [ST_ASEWKT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-asewkt.md): Converts a GEOMETRY or GEOGRAPHY object into a EWKT(extended well-known-text) format representation.
      - [ST_ASGEOJSON](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-asgeojson.md): Converts a GEOMETRY or GEOGRAPHY object into a GeoJSON representation.
      - [ST_ASTEXT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-astext.md): Alias for ST_ASWKT.
      - [ST_ASWKB](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-aswkb.md): Converts a GEOMETRY or GEOGRAPHY object into a WKB(well-known-binary) format representation.
      - [ST_ASWKT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-aswkt.md): Converts a GEOMETRY or GEOGRAPHY object into a WKT(well-known-text) format representation.
      - [ST_AZIMUTH](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-azimuth.md): Returns the azimuth in radians of the line segment from one Point to another, measured clockwise from the positive Y-axis (north). Returns NULL if the two points are identical.
      - [ST_BUFFER](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-buffer.md): Returns a GEOMETRY representing all points whose distance from the input geometry is less than or equal to the specified distance. The result is a MultiPolygon or NULL.
      - [ST_CENTROID](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-centroid.md): Returns the centroid of a GEOMETRY object.
      - [ST_CONTAINS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-contains.md): Returns TRUE if the second GEOMETRY object is completely inside the first GEOMETRY object.
      - [ST_CONVEXHULL](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-convexhull.md): Returns the convex hull of a GEOMETRY object.
      - [ST_COVEREDBY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-coveredby.md): Returns TRUE if no point in the first GEOMETRY object lies outside the second GEOMETRY object.
      - [ST_COVERS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-covers.md): Returns TRUE if no point in the second GEOMETRY object lies outside the first GEOMETRY object.
      - [ST_DIFFERENCE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-difference.md): Returns the part of the first GEOMETRY object that is not covered by the second GEOMETRY object.
      - [ST_DIMENSION](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-dimension.md): Return the dimension for a geometry object. The dimension of a GEOMETRY or GEOGRAPHY object is.
      - [ST_DISJOINT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-disjoint.md): Returns TRUE if two GEOMETRY objects do not intersect.
      - [ST_DISTANCE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-distance.md): Returns the minimum distance between two objects. For GEOMETRY inputs, the function uses Euclidean distance. For GEOGRAPHY inputs, the function uses haversine distance.
      - [ST_DWITHIN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-dwithin.md): Returns TRUE if two GEOMETRY objects are within the specified Euclidean distance.
      - [ST_ENDPOINT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-endpoint.md): Returns the last Point in a LineString.
      - [ST_ENVELOPE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-envelope.md): Returns the minimum bounding rectangle of a GEOMETRY object as a polygon.
      - [ST_EQUALS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-equals.md): Returns TRUE if two GEOMETRY objects are spatially equal.
      - [ST_GEOGETRYFROMWKB](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-geogetryfromwkb.md): Alias for ST_GEOGRAPHYFROMWKB.
      - [ST_GEOGFROMEWKB](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-geogfromewkb.md): Alias for ST_GEOGRAPHYFROMWKB.
      - [ST_GEOGFROMGEOHASH](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-geogfromgeohash.md): Returns a GEOGRAPHY object for the polygon that represents the boundaries of a geohash.
      - [ST_GEOGFROMTEXT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-geogfromtext.md): Alias for ST_GEOGRAPHYFROMWKT.
      - [ST_GEOGFROMWKB](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-geogfromwkb.md): Alias for ST_GEOGRAPHYFROMWKB.
      - [ST_GEOGFROMWKT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-geogfromwkt.md): Alias for ST_GEOGRAPHYFROMWKT.
      - [ST_GEOGPOINTFROMGEOHASH](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-geogpointfromgeohash.md): Returns a GEOGRAPHY object for the point that represents center of a geohash.
      - [ST_GEOGRAPHYFROMEWKT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-geographyfromewkt.md): Alias for ST_GEOGRAPHYFROMWKT.
      - [ST_GEOGRAPHYFROMTEXT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-geographyfromtext.md): Alias for ST_GEOGRAPHYFROMWKT.
      - [ST_GEOGRAPHYFROMWKB](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-geographyfromwkb.md): Parses a WKB(well-known-binary) or EWKB(extended well-known-binary) input and returns a value of type GEOGRAPHY.
      - [ST_GEOGRAPHYFROMWKT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-geographyfromwkt.md): Parses a WKT(well-known-text) or EWKT(extended well-known-text) input and returns a value of type GEOGRAPHY.
      - [ST_GEOHASH](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-geohash.md): Returns the geohash string for a GEOMETRY or GEOGRAPHY value and supports optional precision to control result granularity.
      - [ST_GEOM_POINT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-geom-point.md): Alias for ST_MAKEGEOMPOINT.
      - [ST_GEOMETRYFROMEWKB](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-geometryfromewkb.md): Alias for ST_GEOMTRYFROMWKB.
      - [ST_GEOMETRYFROMEWKT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-geometryfromewkt.md): Alias for ST_GEOMTRYFROMWKT.
      - [ST_GEOMETRYFROMTEXT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-geometryfromtext.md): Alias for ST_GEOMETRYFROMWKT.
      - [ST_GEOMETRYFROMWKB](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-geometryfromwkb.md): Parses a WKB(well-known-binary) or EWKB(extended well-known-binary) input and returns a value of type GEOMETRY.
      - [ST_GEOMETRYFROMWKT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-geometryfromwkt.md): Parses a WKT(well-known-text) or EWKT(extended well-known-text) input and returns a value of type GEOMETRY.
      - [ST_GEOMFROMEWKB](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-geomfromewkb.md): Alias for ST_GEOMTRYFROMWKB.
      - [ST_GEOMFROMEWKT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-geomfromewkt.md): Alias for ST_GEOMTRYFROMWKT.
      - [ST_GEOMFROMGEOHASH](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-geomfromgeohash.md): Returns a GEOMETRY object for the polygon that represents the boundaries of a geohash.
      - [ST_GEOMFROMTEXT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-geomfromtext.md): Alias for ST_GEOMTRYFROMWKT.
      - [ST_GEOMFROMWKB](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-geomfromwkb.md): Alias for ST_GEOMTRYFROMWKB.
      - [ST_GEOMFROMWKT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-geomfromwkt.md): Alias for ST_GEOMTRYFROMWKT.
      - [ST_GEOMPOINTFROMGEOHASH](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-geompointfromgeohash.md): Returns a GEOMETRY object for the point that represents center of a geohash.
      - [ST_HAUSDORFFDISTANCE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-hausdorffdistance.md): Returns the discrete Hausdorff distance between two GEOMETRY objects. This measures how far apart two geometries are by finding the greatest distance from any vertex in one object to the nearest vertex in the other.
      - [ST_HILBERT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-hilbert.md): Encodes a GEOMETRY or GEOGRAPHY object into a Hilbert curve index.
      - [ST_INTERSECTION](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-intersection.md): Returns the shared part of two GEOMETRY objects.
      - [ST_INTERSECTS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-intersects.md): Returns TRUE if two GEOMETRY objects share any portion of space.
      - [ST_ISVALID](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-isvalid.md): Returns TRUE if the GEOMETRY object is geometrically valid as defined by the OGC specification.
      - [ST_LENGTH](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-length.md): Returns the Euclidean length of the LineString(s) in a GEOMETRY or GEOGRAPHY object.
      - [ST_MAKE_LINE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-make-line.md): Alias for ST_MAKELINE.
      - [ST_MAKEGEOMPOINT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-makegeompoint.md): Constructs a GEOMETRY object that represents a Point with the specified longitude and latitude.
      - [ST_MAKELINE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-makeline.md): Constructs a GEOMETRY or GEOGRAPHY object that represents a line connecting the points in the input two GEOMETRY or GEOGRAPHY objects.
      - [ST_MAKEPOINT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-makepoint.md): Constructs a GEOGRAPHY object that represents a Point with the specified longitude and latitude.
      - [ST_MAKEPOLYGON](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-makepolygon.md): Constructs a GEOMETRY or GEOGRAPHY object that represents a Polygon without holes. The function uses the specified LineString as the outer loop.
      - [ST_MAKEPOLYGONORIENTED](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-makepolygonoriented.md): Creates a Polygon from a LineString input, preserving the vertex order as given. Unlike ST_MAKEPOLYGON, this function does not reorder vertices to enforce a specific winding direction.
      - [ST_NPOINTS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-npoints.md): Returns the number of points in a GEOMETRY or GEOGRAPHY object.
      - [ST_NUMPOINTS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-numpoints.md): Alias for ST_NPOINTS.
      - [ST_PERIMETER](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-perimeter.md): Returns the perimeter of polygon(s) in a GEOMETRY object, measured in the units of the coordinate system.
      - [ST_POINT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-point.md): Alias for ST_MAKEPOINT.
      - [ST_POINTN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-pointn.md): Returns a Point at a specified index in a LineString.
      - [ST_POLYGON](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-polygon.md): Alias for ST_MAKEPOLYGON.
      - [ST_SETSRID](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-setsrid.md): Returns a GEOMETRY object that has its SRID (spatial reference system identifier) set to the specified value. This Function only change the SRID without affecting the coordinates of the object. If you also need to change the coordinates to match the new SRS (spatial reference system), use ST_TRANSFORM instead.
      - [ST_SIMPLIFY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-simplify.md): Returns a simplified version of a GEOMETRY object by removing vertices where the distance to the resulting edge is within the specified tolerance. Uses the Ramer-Douglas-Peucker algorithm.
      - [ST_SRID](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-srid.md): Returns the SRID (spatial reference system identifier) of a GEOMETRY or GEOGRAPHY object.
      - [ST_STARTPOINT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-startpoint.md): Returns the first Point in a LineString.
      - [ST_SYMDIFFERENCE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-symdifference.md): Returns the non-overlapping parts of two GEOMETRY objects.
      - [ST_TRANSFORM](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-transform.md): Converts a GEOMETRY object from one spatial reference system (SRS) to another. If you just need to change the SRID without changing the coordinates (e.g. if the SRID was incorrect), use ST_SETSRID instead.
      - [ST_UNION](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-union.md): Returns the combined GEOMETRY made from two input GEOMETRY objects.
      - [ST_WITHIN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-within.md): Returns TRUE if the first GEOMETRY object is completely within the second GEOMETRY object.
      - [ST_X](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-x.md): Returns the longitude (X coordinate) of a Point represented by a GEOMETRY or GEOGRAPHY object.
      - [ST_XMAX](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-xmax.md): Returns the maximum longitude (X coordinate) of all points contained in the specified GEOMETRY or GEOGRAPHY object.
      - [ST_XMIN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-xmin.md): Returns the minimum longitude (X coordinate) of all points contained in the specified GEOMETRY or GEOGRAPHY object.
      - [ST_Y](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-y.md): Returns the latitude (Y coordinate) of a Point represented by a GEOMETRY or GEOGRAPHY object.
      - [ST_YMAX](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-ymax.md): Returns the maximum latitude (Y coordinate) of all points contained in the specified GEOMETRY or GEOGRAPHY object.
      - [ST_YMIN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/st-ymin.md): Returns the minimum latitude (Y coordinate) of all points contained in the specified GEOMETRY or GEOGRAPHY object.
      - [STRING_TO_H3](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/string-to-h3.md): Converts the string representation to H3 (uint64) representation.
      - [TO_GEOGRAPHY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/to-geography.md): Parses an input and returns a value of type GEOGRAPHY.
      - [TO_GEOMETRY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/geometry.md): Parses an input and returns a value of type GEOMETRY.
      - [TO_STRING](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/string-geospatial.md): Converts a GEOMETRY object into a String representation. The display format of the output data is controlled by the geometry_output_format setting, which contains the following types.
    - Full-Text Search Functions
      - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/full-text-search-functions.md): TiDB Cloud Lake's full-text search functions deliver search-engine-style filtering for semi-structured VARIANT data and plain text columns that are indexed with an inverted index. They are ideal for AI-generated metadata—such as perception results from autonomous-driving video frames—stored alongside your assets.
      - [MATCH](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/match.md): Searches indexed columns for keyword matches and can be used only in a WHERE clause.
      - [QUERY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/query.md): Filters rows with a Lucene-style query against columns that have an inverted index and supports dot notation for nested VARIANT fields.
      - [SCORE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/score.md): Returns the relevance score for rows matched by inverted-index search conditions.
    - Structured & Semi-Structured
      - [Structured & Semi-Structured Functions](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/structured-semi-structured-functions.md): Structured and semi-structured functions in TiDB Cloud Lake enable efficient processing of arrays, objects, maps, JSON, and other structured data formats. These functions provide comprehensive capabilities for creating, parsing, querying, transforming, and manipulating structured and semi-structured data.
      - JSON Functions
        - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/json-functions-overview.md): This section provides reference information for JSON functions in TiDB Cloud Lake. JSON functions enable parsing, validation, querying, and manipulation of JSON data structures.
        - [CHECK_JSON](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/check-json.md): Checks the validity of a JSON document. If the input string is a valid JSON document or a NULL, the output is NULL. If the input cannot be translated to a valid JSON value, the output string contains the error message.
        - [GET](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/get.md): Extracts value from a Variant that contains ARRAY by index, or a Variant that contains OBJECT by field_name. The value is returned as a Variant or NULL if either of the arguments is NULL.
        - [GET_BY_KEYPATH](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/get-by-keypath.md): Extracts a nested value from a VARIANT using a key path string. GET_BY_KEYPATH returns the result as VARIANT, while GET_BY_KEYPATH_STRING returns a STRING.
        - [GET_IGNORE_CASE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/get-ignore-case.md): Extracts value from a VARIANT that contains OBJECT by the field_name. The value is returned as a Variant or NULL if either of the arguments is NULL.
        - [GET_PATH](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/get-path.md): Extracts value from a VARIANT by path_name. The value is returned as a Variant or NULL if either of the arguments is NULL.
        - [JQ](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/jq.md): The JQ function is a set-returning SQL function that allows you to apply jq filters to JSON data stored in Variant columns. With this function, you can process JSON data by applying a specified jq filter, returning the results as a set of rows.
        - [JSON_ARRAY_ELEMENTS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/json-array-elements.md): Extracts the elements from a JSON array, returning them as individual rows in the result set. JSON_ARRAY_ELEMENTS does not recursively expand nested arrays; it treats them as single elements.
        - [JSON_CONTAINS_IN_LEFT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/json-contains-left.md): Tests containment relationships between two VARIANT values.
        - [JSON_EACH](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/json-each.md): Extracts key-value pairs from a JSON object, breaking down the structure into individual rows in the result set. Each row represents a distinct key-value pair derived from the input JSON expression.
        - [JSON_EXISTS_KEY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/json-exists-key.md): Checks whether a JSON object contains one or more keys.
        - [JSON_EXTRACT_PATH_TEXT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/json-extract-path-text.md): Extracts value from a Json string by path_name. The value is returned as a String or NULL if either of the arguments is NULL. This function is equivalent to to_varchar(GET_PATH(PARSE_JSON(JSON), PATH_NAME)).
        - [JSON_PATH_EXISTS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/json-path-exists.md): Checks whether a specified path exists in JSON data.
        - [JSON_PATH_MATCH](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/json-path-match.md): Checks whether a specified JSON path expression matches certain conditions within a JSON data. Please note that the @@ operator is synonymous with this function. For more information, see JSON Operators.
        - [JSON_PATH_QUERY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/json-path-query.md): Get all JSON items returned by JSON path for the specified JSON value.
        - [JSON_PATH_QUERY_ARRAY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/json-path-query-array.md): Get all JSON items returned by JSON path for the specified JSON value and wrap a result into an array.
        - [JSON_PATH_QUERY_FIRST](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/json-path-query-first.md): Get the first JSON item returned by JSON path for the specified JSON value.
        - [JSON_PRETTY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/json-pretty.md): Formats JSON data, making it more readable and presentable. It automatically adds indentation, line breaks, and other formatting to the JSON data for better visual representation.
        - [JSON_STRIP_NULLS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/json-strip-nulls.md): Removes all properties with null values from a JSON object.
        - [JSON_TO_STRING](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/json-to-string.md): Alias for TO_STRING.
        - [JSON_TYPEOF](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/json-typeof.md): Returns the type of the main-level of a JSON structure.
        - [PARSE_JSON](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/parse-json.md): Parses a JSON-formatted string and returns a VARIANT value. Use TRY_PARSE_JSON to return NULL instead of an error for invalid input.
        - [STRIP_NULL_VALUE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/strip-null-value.md): Converts a JSON null value to a SQL NULL value. All other variant values are passed unchanged.
      - Array Functions
        - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-functions.md): This section provides reference information for array functions in TiDB Cloud Lake. Array functions enable creation, manipulation, searching, and transformation of array data structures.
        - [ARRAY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-sql.md): Builds an array literal from the supplied expressions. Each argument is evaluated and stored in order. All elements must be castable to a common type.
        - [ARRAY_AGGREGATE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-aggregate.md): Aggregates elements in the array with an aggregate function.
        - [ARRAY_ANY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-any.md): Returns the first non-NULL element from an array. Equivalent to ARRAY_AGGREGATE(<array>, 'ANY').
        - [ARRAY_APPEND](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-append.md): Appends an element to the end of an array.
        - [ARRAY_APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-approx-count-distinct.md): Returns an approximate count of distinct elements in an array, ignoring NULL values. This uses the same HyperLogLog-based estimator as APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT.
        - [ARRAY_AVG](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-avg.md): Returns the average of the numeric items in an array. NULL elements are ignored; non-numeric values raise an error.
        - [ARRAY_COMPACT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-compact.md): Removes all NULL values from an array.
        - [ARRAY_CONCAT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-concat.md): Concats two arrays.
        - [ARRAY_CONSTRUCT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-construct.md): Creates a JSON array with specified values.
        - [ARRAY_CONTAINS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-contains.md): Returns true if the array contains the specified element.
        - [ARRAY_COUNT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-count.md): Counts the non-NULL elements in an array.
        - [ARRAY_DISTINCT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-distinct.md): Removes duplicate elements from a JSON array and returns an array with only distinct elements.
        - [ARRAY_EXCEPT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-except.md): Returns a new JSON array containing the elements from the first JSON array that are not present in the second JSON array.
        - [ARRAY_FILTER](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-filter.md): Filters elements from a JSON array based on a specified Lambda expression, returning only the elements that satisfy the condition. For more information about Lambda expression, see Lambda Expressions.
        - [ARRAY_FLATTEN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-flatten.md): Flattens a nested array into a single-dimensional array.
        - [ARRAY_GENERATE_RANGE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-generate-range.md): Builds an array of evenly spaced integers between a start and end value. The end bound is exclusive.
        - [ARRAY_GET](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-get.md): Alias for GET.
        - [ARRAY_INDEXOF](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-indexof.md): Returns the index of the first occurrence of an element in an array.
        - [ARRAY_INSERT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-insert.md): Inserts a value into a JSON array at the specified index and returns the updated JSON array.
        - [ARRAY_INTERSECTION](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-intersection.md): Returns the common elements between two JSON arrays.
        - [ARRAY_KURTOSIS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-kurtosis.md): Returns the excess kurtosis of the numeric values in an array. NULL elements are ignored; non-numeric elements raise an error.
        - [ARRAY_MAX](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-max.md): Returns the largest numeric value in an array. NULL elements are skipped; non-numeric values cause an error.
        - [ARRAY_MEDIAN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-median.md): Returns the median of the numeric values in an array. NULL elements are ignored.
        - [ARRAY_MIN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-min.md): Returns the smallest numeric value in an array. NULL elements are skipped; non-numeric values cause an error.
        - [ARRAY_OVERLAP](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-overlap.md): Checks if there is any overlap between two JSON arrays and returns true if there are common elements; otherwise, it returns false.
        - [ARRAY_PREPEND](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-prepend.md): Prepends an element to the beginning of an array.
        - [ARRAY_REDUCE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-reduce.md): Reduces a JSON array to a single value by applying a specified Lambda expression. For more information about Lambda expression, see Lambda Expressions.
        - [ARRAY_REMOVE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-remove.md): Removes all occurrences of an element from an array.
        - [ARRAY_REMOVE_FIRST](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-remove-first.md): Removes the first occurrence of an element from an array.
        - [ARRAY_REMOVE_LAST](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-remove-last.md): Removes the last occurrence of an element from an array.
        - [ARRAY_REVERSE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-reverse.md): Reverses the order of elements in an array.
        - [ARRAY_SIZE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-size.md): Returns the length of an array, counting NULL elements.
        - [ARRAY_SKEWNESS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-skewness.md): Returns the skewness of numeric values in an array. NULL items are ignored; non-numeric items raise an error.
        - [ARRAY_SLICE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-slice.md): Extracts a sub-array using slice between start and end arguments.
        - [ARRAY_SORT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-sort.md): Sorts the elements of an array. By default, ARRAY_SORT orders ascending and places NULL values last. Use the explicit variants to control order and NULL placement.
        - [ARRAY_STDDEV_POP](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-stddev-pop.md): Computes the population standard deviation of numeric array values. NULL entries are ignored; non-numeric entries raise an error.
        - [ARRAY_STDDEV_SAMP](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-stddev-samp.md): Computes the sample standard deviation of numeric array values. NULL items are ignored; non-numeric entries raise an error.
        - [ARRAY_SUM](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-sum.md): Sums the numeric elements in an array. NULL items are skipped, and non-numeric values raise an error.
        - [ARRAY_TO_STRING](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-to-string.md): Concatenates the string elements of an array into a single string, separated by a delimiter. NULL elements are skipped.
        - [JSON_ARRAY_TRANSFORM](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/json-array-transform.md): Transforms each element of a JSON array using a specified transformation Lambda expression. For more information about Lambda expression, see Lambda Expressions.
        - [ARRAY_UNIQUE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/array-unique.md): Returns the number of unique elements in the array.
        - [ARRAYS_ZIP](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/arrays-zip.md): Merges multiple arrays into a single array tuple.
        - [CONTAINS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/contains.md): Checks if the array contains a specific element.
        - [GET](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/get-sql.md): Returns an element from an array by index (1-based).
        - [RANGE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/range.md): Returns an array collected by [start, end).
        - [SLICE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/slice.md): Extracts a slice from the array by index (1-based).
        - [UNNEST](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/unnest.md): Unnests the array and returns the set of elements.
      - Object Functions
        - [Object Functions](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/object-functions.md): This section provides reference information for object functions in TiDB Cloud Lake. Object functions enable creation, manipulation, and extraction of information from JSON object data structures.
        - [OBJECT_CONSTRUCT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/object-construct.md): Creates a JSON object with keys and values.
        - [OBJECT_CONSTRUCT_KEEP_NULL](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/object-construct-keep-null.md): Creates a JSON object with keys and values.
        - [OBJECT_DELETE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/object-delete.md): Deletes specified keys from a JSON object and returns the modified object. If a specified key doesn't exist in the object, it is ignored.
        - [OBJECT_INSERT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/object-insert.md): Inserts or updates a key-value pair in a JSON object.
        - [OBJECT_KEYS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/object-keys.md): Returns the keys of the outermost JSON object as an array of strings.
        - [OBJECT_PICK](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/object-pick.md): Creates a new JSON object containing only the specified keys from the input JSON object. If a specified key doesn't exist in the input object, it is omitted from the result.
      - Map Functions
        - [Map Functions](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/map-functions.md): This section provides reference information for the map functions in TiDB Cloud Lake. Map functions allow you to create, manipulate, and extract information from map data structures (key-value pairs).
        - [MAP_CAT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/map-cat.md): Returns the concatenatation of two MAPs.
        - [MAP_CONTAINS_KEY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/map-contains-key.md): Determines whether the specified MAP contains the specified key.
        - [MAP_DELETE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/map-delete.md): Returns an existing MAP with one or more keys removed.
        - [MAP_FILTER](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/map-filter.md): Filters key-value pairs in a JSON object based on a specified condition, defined using a lambda expression.
        - [MAP_INSERT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/map-insert.md): Returns a new MAP consisting of the input MAP with a new key-value pair inserted (an existing key updated with a new value).
        - [MAP_KEYS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/map-keys.md): Returns the keys in a map.
        - [MAP_PICK](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/map-pick.md): Returns a new MAP containing the specified key-value pairs from an existing MAP.
        - [MAP_SIZE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/map-size.md): Returns the size of a MAP.
        - [MAP_TRANSFORM_KEYS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/map-transform-keys.md): Applies a transformation to each key in a JSON object using a lambda expression.
        - [MAP_TRANSFORM_VALUES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/map-transform-values.md): Applies a transformation to each value in a JSON object using a lambda expression.
        - [MAP_VALUES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/map-values.md): Returns the values in a map.
      - Type Conversion
        - [AS_ARRAY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/as-array.md): Strict casting VARIANT values to ARRAY data type. If the input data type is not VARIANT, the output is NULL. If the type of value in the VARIANT does not match the output value, the output is NULL.
        - [AS_BINARY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/as-binary.md): Strict casting VARIANT values to BINARY data type. If the input data type is not VARIANT, the output is NULL. If the type of value in the VARIANT does not match the output value, the output is NULL.
        - [AS_BOOLEAN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/as-boolean.md): Strict casting VARIANT values to BOOLEAN data type. If the input data type is not VARIANT, the output is NULL. If the type of value in the VARIANT does not match the output value, the output is NULL.
        - [AS_DATE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/as-date.md): Strict casting VARIANT values to DATE data type. If the input data type is not VARIANT, the output is NULL. If the type of value in the VARIANT does not match the output value, the output is NULL.
        - [AS_DECIMAL](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/as-decimal.md): Strict casting VARIANT values to DECIMAL data type. If the input data type is not VARIANT, the output is NULL. If the type of value in the VARIANT does not match the output value, the output is NULL.
        - [AS_FLOAT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/as-float.md): Strict casting VARIANT values to DOUBLE data type. If the input data type is not VARIANT, the output is NULL. If the type of value in the VARIANT does not match the output value, the output is NULL.
        - [AS_INTEGER](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/as-integer.md): Strict casting VARIANT values to BIGINT data type. If the input data type is not VARIANT, the output is NULL. If the type of value in the VARIANT does not match the output value, the output is NULL.
        - [AS_OBJECT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/as-object.md): Strict casting VARIANT values to OBJECT data type. If the input data type is not VARIANT, the output is NULL. If the type of value in the VARIANT does not match the output value, the output is NULL.
        - [AS_STRING](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/as-string.md): Strict casting VARIANT values to VARCHAR data type. If the input data type is not VARIANT, the output is NULL. If the type of value in the VARIANT does not match the output value, the output is NULL.
        - [Type Conversion Functions](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/type-conversion-functions.md): This section provides reference information for type conversion functions in TiDB Cloud Lake. These functions enable strict casting of VARIANT values to other SQL data types.
      - Type Predicate
        - [Type Predicate Functions](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/type-predicate-functions.md): This section provides reference information for type predicate functions in TiDB Cloud Lake. These functions enable type checking, validation, and conversion of JSON values.
        - [IS_ARRAY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/is-array.md): Checks if the input value is a JSON array. Please note that a JSON array is not the same as the ARRAY data type. A JSON array is a data structure commonly used in JSON, representing an ordered collection of values enclosed within square brackets []. It is a flexible format for organizing and exchanging various data types, including strings, numbers, booleans, objects, and nulls.
        - [IS_BOOLEAN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/is-boolean.md): Checks if the input JSON value is a boolean.
        - [IS_FLOAT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/is-float.md): Checks if the input JSON value is a float.
        - [IS_INTEGER](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/is-integer.md): Checks if the input JSON value is an integer.
        - [IS_NULL_VALUE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/is-null-value.md): Checks whether the input value is a JSON null. Please note that this function examines JSON null, not SQL NULL. To check if a value is SQL NULL, use IS_NULL.
        - [IS_OBJECT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/is-object.md): Checks if the input value is a JSON object.
        - [IS_STRING](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/is-string.md): Checks if the input JSON value is a string.
    - Vector Functions
      - [COSINE_DISTANCE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/cosine-distance.md): Measuring similarity using the cosine_distance function in TiDB Cloud Lake.
      - [L2_DISTANCE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/l2-distance.md): Calculates the Euclidean (L2) distance between two vectors, measuring the straight-line distance between them in vector space.
      - [L1_DISTANCE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/l1-distance.md): Calculates the Manhattan (L1) distance between two vectors, measuring the sum of absolute differences between corresponding elements.
      - [INNER_PRODUCT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/inner-product.md): Calculates the inner product (dot product) of two vectors, which measures the similarity and projection between vectors.
      - [VECTOR_DIMS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/vector-dims.md): Returns the dimensionality (number of elements) of a vector.
      - [VECTOR_NORM](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/vector-norm.md): Calculates the L2 norm (Euclidean norm) of a vector, which represents the length or magnitude of the vector.
      - [Vector Functions](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/vector-functions.md): Vector functions in TiDB Cloud Lake for vector operations and analysis.
    - Hash Functions
      - [BLAKE3](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/blake.md): Calculates a BLAKE3 256-bit checksum for a string. The value is returned as a string of 64 hexadecimal digits or NULL if the argument was NULL.
      - [CITY64WITHSEED](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/city-withseed.md): Calculates a City64WithSeed 64-bit hash for a string.
      - [Hash Functions](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/hash-functions.md): This page provides a comprehensive overview of Hash functions in TiDB Cloud Lake, organized by functionality for easy reference.
      - [MD5](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/md.md): Calculates an MD5 128-bit checksum for a string. The value is returned as a string of 32 hexadecimal digits or NULL if the argument was NULL.
      - [SHA](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/sha.md): Calculates an SHA-1 160-bit checksum for the string, as described in RFC 3174 (Secure Hash Algorithm). The value is returned as a string of 40 hexadecimal digits or NULL if the argument was NULL.
      - [SHA1](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/sha-sql.md): Alias for SHA.
      - [SHA2](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/sha-functions.md): Calculates the SHA-2 family of hash functions (SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384, and SHA-512). If the hash length is not one of the permitted values, the return value is NULL. Otherwise, the function result is a hash value containing the desired number of bits as a string of hexadecimal digits.
      - [SIPHASH](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/siphash.md): Alias for SIPHASH64.
      - [SIPHASH64](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/siphash-sql.md): Produces a 64-bit SipHash hash value.
      - [XXHASH32](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/xxhash.md): Calculates an xxHash32 32-bit hash value for a string. The value is returned as a UInt32 or NULL if the argument was NULL.
      - [XXHASH64](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/xxhash-sql.md): Calculates an xxHash64 64-bit hash value for a string. The value is returned as a UInt64 or NULL if the argument was NULL.
    - UUID Functions
      - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/uuid-functions.md): This page provides reference information for the UUID-related functions in TiDB Cloud Lake. These functions generate and work with Universally Unique Identifiers (UUIDs).
      - [GEN_RANDOM_UUID](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/gen-random-uuid.md): Generates a random UUID based on version 7, starting from version 1.2.658. Previously, this function generated UUIDs based on version 4.
      - [UUID](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/uuid-sql.md): Alias for GEN_RANDOM_UUID.
    - IP Address Functions
      - [IP Address Functions](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/ip-address-functions.md): This page provides reference information for the IP address-related functions in TiDB Cloud Lake. These functions help convert between string and numeric representations of IP addresses.
      - [INET_ATON](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/inet-aton.md): Converts an IPv4 address to a 32-bit integer.
      - [INET_NTOA](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/inet-ntoa.md): Converts a 32-bit integer to an IPv4 address.
      - [IPV4_NUM_TO_STRING](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/ipv4-num-to-string.md): Alias for INET_NTOA.
      - [IPV4_STRING_TO_NUM](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/ipv4-string-to-num.md): Alias for INET_ATON.
      - [TRY_INET_ATON](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/try-inet-aton.md): try_inet_aton function is used to take the dotted-quad representation of an IPv4 address as a string and returns the numeric value of the given IP address in form of an integer.
      - [TRY_INET_NTOA](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/try-inet-ntoa.md): Takes an IPv4 address in network byte order and then returns the address as a dotted-quad string representation.
      - [TRY_IPV4_NUM_TO_STRING](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/try-ipv4-num-to-string.md): Alias for TRY_INET_NTOA.
      - [TRY_IPV4_STRING_TO_NUM](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/try-ipv4-string-to-num.md): Alias for TRY_INET_ATON.
    - Context Functions
      - [CONNECTION_ID](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/connection-id.md): Returns the connection ID for the current connection.
      - [CURRENT_CATALOG](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/current-catalog.md): Returns the name of the catalog currently in use for the session.
      - [CURRENT_USER](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/current-user.md): Returns the user name and host name combination for the account that the server used to authenticate the current client. This account determines your access privileges. The return value is a string in the utf8 character set.
      - [DATABASE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/database-function.md): Returns the name of the currently selected database. If no database is selected, then this function returns default.
      - [Context Functions](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/context-functions.md): This page provides reference information for the context-related functions in TiDB Cloud Lake. These functions return information about the current session, database, or system context.
      - [LAST_QUERY_ID](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/last-query-id.md): Returns the ID of a query in the current session based on its order.
      - [VERSION](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/version.md): Returns the current version of LakeQuery.
    - System Functions
      - [CLUSTERING_INFORMATION](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/clustering-information.md): Returns clustering information of a table.
      - [FUSE_BLOCK](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/fuse-block.md): Returns the block information of the latest or specified snapshot of a table. For more information about what is block in TiDB Cloud Lake, see What are Snapshot, Segment, and Block?.
      - [FUSE_COLUMN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/fuse-column.md): Returns the column information of the latest or specified snapshot of a table. For more information about what is block in TiDB Cloud Lake, see What are Snapshot, Segment, and Block?.
      - [FUSE_ENCODING](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/fuse-encoding.md): Returns the encoding types applied to a specific column within a table. It helps you understand how data is compressed and stored in a native format within the table.
      - [FUSE_SEGMENT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/fuse-segment.md): Returns the segment information of a specified table snapshot. For more information about what is segment in TiDB Cloud Lake, see What are Snapshot, Segment, and Block?.
      - [FUSE_SNAPSHOT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/fuse-snapshot.md): Returns the snapshot information of a table. For more information about what is snapshot in TiDB Cloud Lake, see What are Snapshot, Segment, and Block?.
      - [FUSE_STATISTIC](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/fuse-statistic.md): note This function is deprecated. Use SHOW STATISTICS instead to view table statistics..
      - [FUSE_TAG](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/fuse-tag.md): Returns the snapshot tags of a table. For more information about snapshot tags, see Snapshot Tags.
      - [FUSE_TIME_TRAVEL_SIZE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/fuse-time-travel-size.md): Calculates the storage size of historical data (for Time Travel) for tables.
      - [FUSE_VIRTUAL_COLUMN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/fuse-virtual-column.md): Returns the virtual column information of the latest or specified snapshot of a table. For details, see Virtual Column.
      - [System Functions](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-functions-sql.md): This page provides reference information for the system-related functions in TiDB Cloud Lake. These functions help you analyze and monitor the internal storage and performance aspects of your TiDB Cloud Lake deployment.
    - Table Functions
      - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/table-functions.md): This page provides reference information for the table functions in TiDB Cloud Lake. Table functions return a set of rows (similar to a table) and can be used in the FROM clause of a query.
      - [INFER_SCHEMA](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/infer-schema.md): Automatically detects the file metadata schema and retrieves the column definitions.
      - [INSPECT_PARQUET](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/inspect-parquet.md): Retrieves a table of comprehensive metadata from a staged Parquet file, including the following columns.
      - [LIST_STAGE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/list-stage.md): Lists files in a stage. This allows you to filter files in a stage based on their extensions and obtain comprehensive details about each file. The function is similar to the DDL command LIST STAGE FILES, but provides you the flexibility to retrieve specific file information with the SELECT statement, such as file name, size, MD5 hash, last modified timestamp, and creator, rather than all file information.
      - [GENERATE_SERIES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/generate-series.md): Generates a dataset starting from a specified point, ending at another specified point, and optionally with an incrementing value. The GENERATE_SERIES function works with the following data types.
      - [FLATTEN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/flatten.md): Transforms nested JSON or array data into a tabular format, where each element or field is represented as a separate row.
      - [SYSTEM$FUSE_AMEND](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/system-fuse-amend.md): Recovers table data from S3-compatible object storage.
      - [FUSE_VACUUM_TEMPORARY_TABLE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/fuse-vacuum-temporary-table.md): Temporary tables are typically cleaned up automatically at session end (details in CREATE TEMP TABLE). However, this process can fail due to events like query node crashes or abnormal session terminations, leaving orphaned temporary files.
      - [ICEBERG_MANIFEST](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/iceberg-manifest.md): Returns metadata about manifest files of an Iceberg table, including file paths, partitioning details, and snapshot associations.
      - [ICEBERG_SNAPSHOT](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/iceberg-snapshot.md): Returns metadata about snapshots of an Iceberg table, including information about data changes, operations, and summary statistics.
      - [POLICY_REFERENCES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/policy-references.md): Returns the associations between security policies (Masking Policy or Row Access Policy) and tables/views. You can query by policy name to find all tables using it, or by table name to find all policies applied to it.
      - [RESULT_SCAN](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/result-scan.md): Retrieves the cached result of a previous query by its query ID.
      - [SYSTEM$SET_CACHE_CAPACITY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/set-cache-capacity.md): Adjusts the capacity of a named cache at runtime.
      - [SHOW_GRANTS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-grants-sql.md): Lists privileges granted to roles, role assignments for users, or privileges on a specific object.
      - [SHOW_VARIABLES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/show-variables-sql.md): Displays all session variables and their details, such as names, values, and types.
      - [STREAM_STATUS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/stream-status.md): Provides information about the status of a specified stream, yielding a single-column result (has_data) that can take on values of true or false.
      - [TAG_REFERENCES](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/tag-references.md): Returns all tags assigned to a specified database object.
      - [TASK_HISTORY](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/task-history.md): Displays task running history given variables.
    - Sequence Functions
      - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/sequence-functions-overview.md): This section provides reference information for the sequence functions in TiDB Cloud Lake. Sequence functions allow you to work with sequence objects, which generate unique, auto-incrementing numeric values.
      - [NEXTVAL](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/nextval.md): Retrieves the next value from a sequence.
    - Data Anonymization Functions
      - [FEISTEL_OBFUSCATE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/feistel-obfuscate.md): Deterministically obfuscate integers (e.g. IDs or phone numbers) while preserving bit length and value cardinality so joins still work.
      - [Data Anonymization Functions](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/data-anonymization-functions.md): Data anonymization is the process of altering or removing personally identifiable information (PII) from data sets to protect individual privacy. Its goal is to transform data so it cannot be linked back to specific individuals, while preserving the data's utility for analysis, research, and testing.
      - [MARKOV_GENERATE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/markov-generate.md): Using the model trained by MARKOV_TRAIN to anonymize the dataset.
      - [OBFUSCATE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/obfuscate.md): Dataset anonymization. This is a quick tool, and for more complex scenarios, it is recommended to directly use the underlying function MARKOV_TRAIN, MARKOV_GENERATE, FEISTEL_OBFUSCATE.
    - Test Functions
      - [Test Functions](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/test-functions.md): This page provides reference information for the test functions in TiDB Cloud Lake. These functions are primarily used for testing and debugging purposes.
      - [SLEEP](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/sleep.md): Sleeps seconds seconds on each data block.
    - Other Functions
      - [Overview](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/other-functions.md): This section collects assorted utilities that do not fit into the major functional groups.
      - [ASSUME_NOT_NULL](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/assume-not-null.md): Results in an equivalent non-Nullable value for a Nullable type. In case the original value is NULL the result is undetermined.
      - [EXISTS](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/exists.md): The exists condition is used in combination with a subquery and is considered "to be met" if the subquery returns at least one row.
      - [GROUPING](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/grouping.md): Returns a bit mask indicating which GROUP BY expressions are not included in the current grouping set. Bits are assigned with the rightmost argument corresponding to the least-significant bit; each bit is 0 if the corresponding expression is included in the grouping criteria of the grouping set generating the current result row, and 1 if it is not included.
      - [HUMANIZE_NUMBER](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/humanize-number.md): Returns a readable number.
      - [HUMANIZE_SIZE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/humanize-size.md): Returns the readable size with a suffix(KiB, MiB, etc).
      - [READ_FILE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/read-file.md): Reads a file from a stage and returns its raw bytes.
      - [REMOVE_NULLABLE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/remove-nullable.md): Alias for ASSUME_NOT_NULL.
      - [TO_NULLABLE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/nullable.md): Converts a value to its nullable equivalent.
      - [TYPEOF](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/typeof.md): TYPEOF function is used to return the name of a data type.
  - [Stored Procedure & Scripting](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/stored-procedure-scripting.md): Stored procedures in TiDB Cloud Lake let you package SQL logic that runs on the server with access to control flow, variables, cursors, and dynamic statements. This page explains how to create procedures and write the inline scripting that powers them.
- General Reference
  - [Architecture](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/tidb-cloud-lake-architecture.md): TiDB Cloud Lake Architecture.
  - Implementation Deep Dives
    - [Fuse Engine](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/how-fuse-engine-works.md): Fuse Engine is TiDB Cloud Lake's core storage engine, optimized for managing petabyte-scale data efficiently on cloud object storage. By default, tables created in TiDB Cloud Lake automatically use this engine (ENGINE=FUSE). Inspired by Git, its snapshot-based design enables powerful data versioning (like Time Travel) and provides high query performance through advanced pruning and indexing.
    - [Optimizer](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/how-optimizer-works.md): TiDB Cloud Lake's query optimizer orchestrates a series of transformations that turn SQL text into an executable plan. The optimizer builds an abstract representation of the query, enriches it with real-time statistics, applies rule-based rewrites, explores join alternatives, and finally picks the cheapest physical operators.
    - [JSON](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/how-json-variant-works.md): TiDB Cloud Lake reimagines JSON analytics by pairing a native binary layout with automatic JSON indexing so semi-structured data behaves like first-class columns.
    - [Data Sharing](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/how-data-sharing-works.md): Different teams need different parts of the same data. Traditional solutions copy data multiple times - expensive and hard to maintain.
  - [Editions](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/editions.md): TiDB Cloud Lake comes in three editions Personal, Business, and Dedicated, that you can choose from to serve a wide range of needs and ensure optimal performance for different use cases.
  - [Platforms & Regions](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/platforms-regions.md): Learn about the supported cloud platforms and regions for TiDB Cloud Lake.
  - Benchmarks
    - [Data Ingestion Benchmark](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/benchmark-data-ingestion.md): This page presents a benchmark comparison of data ingestion performance and cost between TiDB Cloud Lake and Snowflake, focusing on TPC-H SF100 dataset loading, ClickBench Hits dataset loading, and freshness benchmarks.
    - [TPC-H SF100 Benchmark](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/benchmark-tpch-sf100.md): This guide presents a performance and cost comparison between TiDB Cloud Lake and Snowflake using the TPC-H SF100 dataset. It includes data loading and query execution benchmarks, along with instructions to reproduce the results.
    - [TPC-H SF1000 Benchmark](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/benchmark-tpch-sf1000.md): This guide presents a performance comparison of Small, Medium, and Large TiDB Cloud Lake Warehouses using the TPC-H SF1000 dataset. It includes query execution times for each warehouse size and instructions to reproduce the benchmark results.
- [Support Services](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidbcloudlake/support-services.md): TiDB Cloud Lake provides comprehensive Support Services for our TiDB Cloud Lake users and customers. Our objective is to deliver exceptional support that reflects the TiDB Cloud Lake product's core values – high performance, ease of use, and fast, high-quality results.
